}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n<div class=\"layout\">\n  <aside>\n    <div class=\"brand\"><span class=\"dot\"></span><span>Playbooks</span></div>\n    <p class=\"kicker\">On this page</p>\n    <nav aria-label=\"Table of contents\">\n      <ol>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#business-architecture\">Business Architecture</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#segment-mix\">Segment mix</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#end-market-exposure\">End-market exposure</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#ai-investment-cycle-position\">AI Investment Cycle Position</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#active-catalysts\">Active Catalysts</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#sell-side-disagreement-axes\">Sell-Side Disagreement Axes</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#i-interface-disruption\">(i) Interface disruption</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#ii-monetisation-compression\">(ii) Monetisation compression</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#iii-cost-disruption\">(iii) Cost disruption</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#iv-ecosystem-and-distribution-displacement\">(iv) Ecosystem &amp; distribution</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#v-cloud-differentiation\">(v) Cloud differentiation</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#failure-modes\">Failure Modes</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#ticker-specific-overrides-rationale\">Ticker-Specific Overrides</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h3\"><a href=\"#scenario-axes-design-rationale\"><code>scenario_axes</code> rationale</a></li>\n        <li class=\"h2\"><a href=\"#historical-reset-and-recover-priors\">Historical Priors</a></li>\n      </ol>\n    </nav>\n    <p class=\"kicker\">Status</p>\n    <div class=\"status-block\">MEDIUM confidence · updated 2026-05-18</div>\n  </aside>\n\n  <main>\n    <div class=\"doc-head\">\n      <div class=\"breadcrumbs\">Playbooks · <span>GOOG</span></div>\n      <h1>GOOG Playbook</h1>\n      <div class=\"pill-row\">\n        <span class=\"pill pill-meta\">GOOG</span>\n        <span class=\"pill pill-meta\">MEDIUM confidence</span>\n        <span class=\"pill pill-meta\">2026-05-18</span>\n      </div>\n      <dl class=\"meta-grid\">\n        <dt>Source</dt><dd>playbooks/GOOG.md</dd>\n        <dt>Rendered</dt><dd>2026-05-18</dd>\n        <dt>ticker</dt><dd>GOOG</dd>\n        <dt>last_updated</dt><dd>2026-05-18</dd>\n        <dt>base_wacc</dt><dd>9.0</dd>\n        <dt>growth_ceiling</dt><dd>0.13</dd>\n        <dt>terminal_margin</dt><dd>0.30</dd>\n        <dt>confidence_anchor</dt><dd>MEDIUM</dd>\n        <dt>scenario_axes</dt><dd>bear: growth_ceiling 0.04, terminal_margin 0.22 · bull: growth_ceiling 0.18, terminal_margin 0.32</dd>\n        <dt>bear_narrative</dt><dd>Interface displacement + cost-permanent: AI-native assistants capture commercial-intent query share, revenue-per-search compresses as ad density and CPC (Cost Per Click) fall, and AI serving costs remain structurally elevated. Terminal margin anchors to low-20s; long-run earnings growth converges to low single digits.</dd>\n        <dt>base_narrative</dt><dd>Cost-temporary, monetisation-resilient: AI Overviews and AI Mode keep users inside Google surfaces; capex-to-revenue ratio mean-reverts post-2027 as model efficiency improves; Cloud (GCP) margin expands toward mid-20s. Terminal margin recovers to ~30% SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped FCF (Free Cash Flow) basis as the AI build-cycle normalises.</dd>\n        <dt>bull_narrative</dt><dd>AI amplifier — multiple independent upside vectors: (i) AI Mode + AI Overview monetise at parity-or-better RPM (Revenue Per Mille) vs. classical Search, sustaining revenue-per-query through the interface transition; (ii) GCP TPU + Vertex + Gemini-on-Cloud stack creates durable differentiation vs. AWS/Azure, expanding Cloud margins toward high-20s by FY2028; (iii) Waymo monetisation matures — multi-city fleet revenue and autonomous-driving licensing become a real P&amp;L (Profit and Loss) contributor; (iv) AI capex/revenue ratio declines post-FY2026 as model efficiency improves and capital-intensity normalises toward pre-AI levels; (v) DOJ and EU DMA (Digital Markets Act) remedies stay at conduct-rule margins, preserving default-placement economics in modified form; (vi) Gemini consumer adoption produces measurable first-place-I-ask share gain in high-intent commercial queries, reinforcing platform moat against AI-native alternatives.</dd>\n        <dt>failure_modes</dt><dd>\n          <ul>\n            <li>Interface displacement (structural): multi-quarter monotonic migration of commercial-intent queries to AI-native interfaces. [interface layer]</li>\n            <li>Monetisation compression (structural): AI Overview / AI Mode rollout compresses revenue-per-search durably. [monetisation layer]</li>\n            <li>Cost disruption (structural): AI capex/revenue ratio stays elevated beyond 2028. [cost layer]</li>\n            <li>Distribution remedy: DOJ remedies impair default-placement economics materially. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n            <li>Cloud commoditisation: GCP margins fail to expand durably above mid-teens by 2027. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n            <li>Geo-regulatory contagion: EU DMA / India / other-jurisdiction remedies replicate US erosion. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n          </ul>\n        </dd>\n      </dl>\n    </div>\n\n    <p><strong>Coverage status:</strong> ESTABLISHED · INCUMBENT<br>\n    <strong>Thesis in one line:</strong> AI-search-disruption debate + DOJ distribution-economics remedies + AI capex cost-permanence question — three structurally intertwined uncertainties that generic INCUMBENT/ESTABLISHED defaults cannot price.</p>\n    <hr>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"business-architecture\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">01</span><h2>Business Architecture</h2></header>\n\n      <h3 id=\"segment-mix\">Segment mix (approximate FY2025 basis)</h3>\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Segment</th><th>Revenue share</th><th>Growth trajectory</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>Google Search &amp; Other</td><td>~57%</td><td>Low-to-mid single digits; AI disruption is the structural risk</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>YouTube Ads</td><td>~11%</td><td>Mid-teens; subscription (YouTube Premium) adds a recurring layer</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Google Network (AdSense / AdMob / DV360)</td><td>~9%</td><td>Declining; programmatic ad-tech under AdTech regulatory scrutiny</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Google Cloud (GCP + Workspace)</td><td>~13%</td><td>~28–30% YoY; becoming the second material earnings contributor</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Google Other (Pixel, Play, Maps, subscriptions)</td><td>~5%</td><td>Mid-single digits; hardware margins thin</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Other Bets (Waymo, Verily, etc.)</td><td>~1%</td><td>R&amp;D-stage; not meaningful to near-term FCF</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n\n      <p><strong>Revenue driver mechanics:</strong></p>\n      <ol>\n        <li><strong>Search:</strong> Paid clicks × CPC (Cost Per Click). Absolute quarterly Search CPM (Cost Per Thousand Impressions) and click volumes are not disclosed by Alphabet (noted as OQ6 gap in the engagement-KPI map) — revenue-per-search trend is inferred from total Search &amp; Other revenue YoY, not directly observable. This limits the precision of monetisation-compression monitoring; the playbook does not attempt quarterly KPI tracking.</li>\n        <li><strong>YouTube:</strong> Primarily video ad auction (CPM-based); YouTube Premium subs add a lower-variance recurring line. Ad load and engagement trends are disclosed directionally but not with unit-economics granularity.</li>\n        <li><strong>Cloud:</strong> Committed GCP revenue backlog + Workspace seats. Backlog growth is disclosed quarterly; it is the leading indicator for Cloud revenue trajectory.</li>\n        <li><strong>Other Bets:</strong> Waymo is the only Other Bets asset with a plausible near-term monetisation path (robotaxi per-mile revenue, fleet licensing). Not material to DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) in the base case.</li>\n      </ol>\n\n      <h3 id=\"end-market-exposure\">End-market exposure</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Digital advertising (~77% of revenue):</strong> Cyclical sensitivity to global ad-spend budgets; secular tail risk from AI-interface displacement.</li>\n        <li><strong>Enterprise cloud (~13% of revenue):</strong> GCP + Workspace; less cyclical; differentiated through Gemini integration.</li>\n        <li><strong>Hardware / consumer services (~5%):</strong> Pixel, Google One, Maps API — limited operating leverage.</li>\n      </ul>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"ai-investment-cycle-position\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">02</span><h2>AI Investment Cycle Position</h2></header>\n\n      <p>Alphabet spent ~$91B in FY2025 capex, ~70% AI-attributed per public guidance. This depresses TTM clean FCF margin and creates a two-sided uncertainty that is structurally different from a normal capex cycle trough: the normalisation path depends on <strong>which of two competing margin theses proves correct.</strong></p>\n\n      <p><strong>Path A — cost-temporary (base case):</strong><br>\n      AI model efficiency improves on hardware and software curves (inference cost-per-query falls as TPUs scale and model compression matures). Capex-as-share-of-revenue mean-reverts post-2027 as the build phase completes. Monetisation density per AI-assisted query holds near current levels or improves (AI Overviews maintain ad slots; AI Mode monetises at comparable RPM (Revenue Per Mille) to standard Search). Terminal margin recovers toward 30% SBC-stripped FCF.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Path B — cost-permanent (bear-case terminal margin thesis):</strong><br>\n      AI serving costs do not decay with scale at the rate Path A assumes — either because competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment, or because each AI query is structurally more compute-intensive than a traditional lookup. Simultaneously, AI-style answering reduces click-through rates, compressing ad density and CPC. Revenue growth decelerates while cost stays elevated. Terminal margin stabilises in the low-20s. This is the basis for <code>scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code>.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Base-case choice:</strong> The playbook picks Path A but does not assume the asymmetry away. The <code>terminal_margin</code> base of 30% reflects Path A prevailing. The bear <code>scenario_axes</code> captures Path B as a discrete scenario — not a symmetric delta from base — because interface displacement and cost-permanence cause joint compression of both growth and margin simultaneously, which a symmetric ±multiplier cannot represent.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Normalised-margin anchors:</strong> The <code>terminal_margin</code> base of 30% sits between two reference points. Reported TTM FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin is severely depressed by the AI build cycle — with ~$91B FY2025 capex, capex-blended group FCF margin is in the low-to-mid single digits (approximate; derived from disclosed capex and operating cash flows). On a normalised-capex, SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped basis — stripping the AI-attributed ~$64B capex increment above estimated pre-AI maintenance capex (~$25B) and SBC (~5–6% of revenue per disclosed annual figures) — clean FCF margin is inferred at approximately 22–27%: this is the distressed-floor reference point under Path A's recovery thesis. Search-segment-implied margin is structurally higher: Search &amp; Other at ~57% of revenue is Alphabet's highest-margin segment, with implied margins above 35% plausible given disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income of ~28–30% (approximate; GAAP segment FCF margins are not separately reported — treat these as order-of-magnitude anchors, not precise figures). The 30% base sits between the normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%) and the Search-segment ceiling (~35%+) — a defensible midpoint under Path A.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>AI-capex normalisation signal:</strong> The evidence-gating condition for Path A is a sustained decline in capex/revenue ratio after FY2026, visible across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that re-elevates above FY2025 levels by FY2028 would be evidence for Path B.</p>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"active-catalysts\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">03</span><h2>Active Catalysts</h2></header>\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Catalyst</th><th>Probability</th><th>IV impact</th><th>Direction</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>DOJ Search remedies finalised (default-payment restrictions, Chrome leverage, or divestiture ordered)</td><td>~35% material remedy by end-2027</td><td>−10–20%</td><td>Strongly negative — distribution economics impaired</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>AI Mode Search query-mix data disclosed showing CPC stability</td><td>~40% by end-2026</td><td>+5–10%</td><td>Positive — monetisation-compression bear case weakened</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>GCP margin print sustains above 15% for 2+ consecutive quarters</td><td>~55% by end-2027</td><td>+5–8%</td><td>Positive — Cloud-as-earnings-contributor thesis validated</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Gemini consumer adoption milestone (measurable first-place-I-ask share shift, third-party data)</td><td>~30% by end-2027</td><td>+3–7%</td><td>Positive — platform-lock thesis reinforced</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>AdTech structural separation ruling (forced unwind of ad-exchange vertical integration)</td><td>~25%</td><td>−8–15%</td><td>Negative — Network segment economics impaired</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>AI-native interface (ChatGPT / Perplexity / Claude) captures measurable commercial-intent query share (3rd-party panel data, sustained 2+ quarters)</td><td>~30% by end-2027</td><td>−15–25%</td><td>Strongly negative — interface-displacement thesis fires</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Waymo monetisation milestone (revenue-generating fleet in 3+ cities at scale)</td><td>~40% by end-2027</td><td>+2–5%</td><td>Modest positive — Other Bets optionality partially realised</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Capex/revenue ratio trajectory: FY2027 &lt; FY2026 for two consecutive years</td><td>~50%</td><td>+8–12%</td><td>Positive — Path A confirmed, terminal-margin re-rate</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"sell-side-disagreement-axes\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">04</span><h2>Sell-Side Disagreement Axes</h2></header>\n\n      <p>Organised by the <strong>4-layer AI-disruption taxonomy</strong> plus Cloud differentiation. Each axis names what distinguishes temporary noise from structural change.</p>\n\n      <h3 id=\"i-interface-disruption\">(i) Interface disruption</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Do AI assistants become the primary discovery and navigation layer, displacing Google Search as the first-place-I-ask interface for high-intent commercial queries?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> AI Overviews and AI Mode keep users inside Google surfaces for the queries that generate ad revenue; \"where do you start a purchase or research query\" surveys remain Google-dominant. Competitors capture curiosity and informational queries, not commercial-intent ones.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> AI-native interfaces (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, in-OS assistants, browser-native AI) capture meaningful share of commercial-intent queries — the queries that actually produce CPC revenue. Users who stop clicking to Google for high-intent searches stop generating ad impressions entirely.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> A single-quarter deceleration in Search revenue growth is noise — ad-cycle effects, macro, seasonality, and mix-shift within Search all produce this. Structural signal requires: monotonic commercial-intent query-share migration <strong>sustained across ≥3 quarters</strong>; \"first-place-I-ask\" data from third-party consumer panels showing a durable shift (not curiosity queries — specifically purchase-research, product-comparison, local-service-intent); revenue-per-search trend declining even in periods of macro-stable ad spend. All three together constitute structural signal; any one alone is insufficient.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"ii-monetisation-compression\">(ii) Monetisation compression</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Even at stable Search query share, does AI-style answering structurally compress revenue-per-search — via fewer ad slots per query, reduced click-through, or lower CPC?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> AI Overviews maintain or improve revenue-per-search through better ad-intent matching; users who get AI answers and then click on ads are higher-intent buyers; blended RPM (Revenue Per Mille) holds or expands.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> AI summaries satisfy the user's need without a click; ad slot count per query falls as above-the-fold content becomes AI-generated; CPC compresses as advertiser competition for fewer slots declines.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> Revenue-per-search trend over ≥2 quarters, filtered against macro ad-cycle movements by comparing to peer ad platforms (Meta, Snap, Pinterest) at the same periods. A revenue-per-search decline that tracks macro peers is cycle noise; one that diverges negatively from peers while the macro environment is stable is monetisation-compression signal. Absolute click volumes and CPM are not disclosed (OQ6 gap), so the observable proxy is total Search revenue growth rate relative to peer ad-platform growth rates.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"iii-cost-disruption\">(iii) Cost disruption</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Does AI inference cost remain structurally elevated, preventing margin recovery even if Search revenue holds?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> Inference cost-per-query declines on TPU hardware scaling and model-efficiency curves (distillation, quantisation, smaller purpose-built models); capex/revenue mean-reverts post-2027; operating leverage reasserts as fixed-cost build phase completes.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> AI serving cost is a permanent elevated line item — each AI query is computationally costlier than a keyword lookup by a structurally different order of magnitude; competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment to match quality; the cost-efficiency gains are real but are competed away in the form of better product rather than margin expansion.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> Capex/revenue ratio trend post-FY2026 across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that declines from FY2025 peak toward pre-AI levels (≤15% of revenue) is Path A signal. A ratio that stabilises above 18% of revenue through FY2028 is Path B signal. Gross-margin segmentation data (if and when disclosed at the Cloud or AI-products segment level) would be the most direct evidence but is not currently available.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"iv-ecosystem-and-distribution-displacement\">(iv) Ecosystem and distribution displacement</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Does regulatory and competitive erosion of Google's distribution advantages structurally weaken the default-placement economics that underpin Search market share?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> Distribution moats hold: Chrome browser default-search leverage continues, Apple default-search-engine payment (~$18–20B/year, market estimate) survives legal scrutiny in modified form, Android OEM agreements sustain Google's first-call position. Regulatory remedies stay at the margins (conduct rules, not structural separation).</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> DOJ remedies materially weaken default-placement economics — payments-for-default restricted or banned, Chrome divested or usage-gated, Android default-app leverage limited. Independent of which specific remedy is imposed: the structural question is whether Google's distribution advantages durably erode. An ecosystem-level erosion would move Search market share on a multi-year lag, not immediately — making it a slow-burn bear case, not a binary one.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> Actual remedies imposed (with material appeals exhausted, not just initial rulings); third-party measurement of default-search-engine market share in the 12–24 months post-remedy implementation. Court rulings that are appealed and do not result in operational changes are procedural noise; operational changes to the Chrome default or the Apple TAC (Traffic Acquisition Cost) payment are structural signal.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"v-cloud-differentiation\">(v) Cloud differentiation</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Is GCP developing durable economic differentiation, or participating in a capital-intensive AI infrastructure cycle where margins normalise to mid-cycle hyperscaler economics?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> TPU + Vertex AI + Gemini-on-Cloud create a stack-level differentiation that justifies sustained pricing power; enterprise customers building Gemini-powered workflows create switching-cost stickiness analogous to AWS-native application lock-in; GCP margin expands sustainably toward AWS/Azure levels (high-20s to low-30s).</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> GCP participates in the AI capex cycle as a capacity provider, but without the enterprise-grade trust, developer ecosystem depth, or data-gravity advantages of AWS or Azure; margins normalise to mid-cycle hyperscaler economics (mid-teens); GCP is a strategic hedge for Alphabet but does not compensate for Search revenue risk.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> GCP operating margin trajectory reported across ≥4 consecutive quarters at scale; pricing power signals from renewal rate commentary and enterprise customer-mix data (disclosed intermittently). GCP margins below 15% by FY2027 would weaken the base-case Cloud offset; margins expanding above 20% by FY2027 would strengthen the bull case.</li>\n      </ul>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"failure-modes\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">05</span><h2>Failure Modes</h2></header>\n\n      <p>These are the thesis-breaking scenarios that the DCF does not capture because they are discrete structural shifts rather than smooth-curve adjustments:</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Interface displacement (structural):</strong> Multi-quarter monotonic migration of commercial-intent queries to AI-native interfaces — invalidates the base revenue growth assumption. This is the failure mode that does not have a historical analogue in Alphabet's operating history: prior Search challengers (Bing, Yahoo relaunch) did not change user behaviour at the interface layer; AI assistants potentially do. [interface layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Monetisation compression (structural):</strong> AI Overview and AI Mode rollout compresses revenue-per-search durably; ad density falls as AI summaries occupy above-the-fold positions; CPC declines as advertiser competition for fewer slots decreases. This failure mode can coexist with stable query volumes — making it harder to detect via search share data alone. [monetisation layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Cost disruption (structural):</strong> AI capex/revenue ratio stays elevated beyond FY2028 with no margin recovery. In conjunction with monetisation compression, this produces joint revenue-and-margin pressure — the scenario captured by <code>scenario_axes.bear</code> compressing both <code>growth_ceiling</code> and <code>terminal_margin</code> simultaneously. [cost layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Distribution remedy:</strong> DOJ remedies impair default-placement economics materially. The specific form matters less than the functional outcome: if Google cannot pay for or mandate default Search placement in Chrome, Android, and Apple Safari, the structural query-share floor is removed. Independent of any single ruling's outcome — the structural impairment of distribution economics is the failure condition, not the legal calendar. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Cloud commoditisation:</strong> GCP margins fail to expand durably above mid-teens by FY2027. This eliminates the optionality embedded in the base case — the assumption that Cloud eventually becomes a material second earnings engine that partially offsets Search risk. If GCP remains a mid-margin business, the base case requires Search to sustain its current earnings contribution with no structural offset. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Geo-regulatory contagion:</strong> EU DMA, India CCI, and other-jurisdiction remedies replicate the distribution-economics erosion pattern outside the US market. The US DOJ case creates a precedent and negotiating template; a coordinated multi-jurisdiction wave of structural remedies could impair non-US revenue streams that are not currently in the bear-case model. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n      </ul>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"ticker-specific-overrides-rationale\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">06</span><h2>Ticker-Specific Overrides (Rationale)</h2></header>\n\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Value</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>base_wacc</code></td>\n            <td>9.0%</td>\n            <td>US 10y ~4.5% + Beta ~1.05 × 5.5% ERP (Equity Risk Premium) ≈ 10.3%. Less ~1.0pp moat-durability discount (dominant Search economics + Cloud share gains remain intact today). Plus ~0.3pp regulatory premium (active DOJ remedies + AdTech + EU DMA + jurisdictional contagion risk). Sits at META parity (9.0%) rather than ASML monopoly level (8.5%) — Search durability is a live contested thesis, unlike ASML's EUV monopoly which has no credible near-term challenger.</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>growth_ceiling</code></td>\n            <td>13%</td>\n            <td>Fallback ceiling when <code>eps_growth_5y</code> is unavailable (current state per yfinance MCP). Below the generic 18% INCUMBENT default because: (a) $4.7T mega-cap mathematics constrain absolute growth, (b) Search (~57% of revenue) grows at ~5–7% and is the dominant segment, (c) Cloud (~13% of revenue) grows at ~28–30% but is not yet large enough to move the blended rate materially. Consensus <code>eps_growth_5y</code> takes precedence when populated; this override is the floor/ceiling for the fallback path only.</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>terminal_margin</code></td>\n            <td>30%</td>\n            <td>SBC-stripped FCF margin assuming Path A (cost-temporary) prevails. TTM clean margin is depressed by the AI build cycle. 30% sits between normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%, approximate; SBC-stripped, normalised-capex basis derived from disclosed segment data — not separately reported) and Search-segment ceiling (~35%+, approximate; inferred from disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income) — a defensible mid-range under the cost-temporary path. Path B (cost-permanent) downside is held discretely in <code>scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code>, not absorbed into the base value. Without <code>scenario_axes</code>, a 30% base-case terminal margin would be overconfident; with it, the base stays clean and the structural asymmetry is priced in the bear DCF.</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>confidence_anchor</code></td>\n            <td>MEDIUM</td>\n            <td>The AI-disruption thesis spans four distinct structural questions (interface / monetisation / cost / ecosystem) that cannot be resolved from current financials. MCP data quality is adequate (4y FCF (Free Cash Flow), SBC, diluted shares present); LOW would be too pessimistic on data quality grounds. Structural-behavioural uncertainty is what caps confidence, not data availability. Below META's HIGH because META's central debate (regulatory) is discrete and binary; GOOG's central debate (interface displacement) is continuous, multi-modal, and decision-relevant in the base case, not just in tail scenarios.</td>\n          </tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n\n      <h3 id=\"scenario-axes-design-rationale\"><code>scenario_axes</code> design rationale</h3>\n      <p>Standard ±multiplier scenarios would produce symmetric bear/bull deltas from the base. GOOG's thesis is structurally asymmetric in a way that requires explicit overrides on both dimensions simultaneously:</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bear case:</strong> Interface displacement causes <strong>joint</strong> compression of growth ceiling (query share migrates) and terminal margin (monetisation compresses + costs stay elevated). A symmetric −5pp terminal-margin delta off 30% (i.e., 25%) understates the joint structural-break shape. <code>bear.growth_ceiling: 0.04</code> anchors below the symmetric multiplier because the bear case is not a cycle trough — it is an interface-layer shift where EPS growth converges toward low single digits. <code>bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code> sits below the TTM-clean FCF margin to reflect the joint structural break, not a recoverable cycle compression.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bull case:</strong> The bull thesis is monetisation-density improvement + Cloud acceleration. <code>bull.growth_ceiling: 0.18</code> matches the upper bound of pre-AI-discount consensus and allows the bull-case DCF to capture upside without being artificially compressed by the 13% fallback. <code>bull.terminal_margin: 0.32</code> is a modest above-base anchor for the scenario where Path A delivers cleanly and AI Overviews monetise at parity to current Search.</li>\n      </ul>\n      <p>Unspecified scenario fields fall back to standard ±multiplier per the loader spec.</p>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"historical-reset-and-recover-priors\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">07</span><h2>Historical Reset-and-Recover Priors</h2></header>\n\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Episode</th><th>Drawdown (approx)</th><th>Catalyst</th><th>Recovery</th><th>Lesson</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr>\n            <td>2022 ad recession + iOS privacy reset</td>\n            <td>~−45% peak-to-trough</td>\n            <td>Macro ad-spend contraction; Apple ATT (App Tracking Transparency) headwinds to ad-targeting quality</td>\n            <td>~12 months; recovery on ad-market rebound and YouTube brand-advertiser return</td>\n            <td>Cyclical ad recessions recover on macro normalisation; the underlying monetisation mechanics remained intact throughout</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td>2023 Bing + ChatGPT integration scare</td>\n            <td>~−15% drawdown</td>\n            <td>Microsoft integrated GPT-4 into Bing; sell-side concern about Search displacement</td>\n            <td>~6 months; recovered as Bing share gains remained marginal and Google announced Bard/Gemini roadmap</td>\n            <td>A credible competitive interface challenge caused a multiple de-rate, but was not sufficient to structurally impair query economics at the monetisation layer</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td>2024–2025 DOJ verdict + AI-Mode launch uncertainty</td>\n            <td>~−20–25% drawdown (approximate)</td>\n            <td>DOJ liability finding in Search distribution case; uncertainty around AI Mode cannibalising Search RPM (Revenue Per Mille)</td>\n            <td>Partial recovery as AI Overviews maintained revenue-per-search in initial disclosed metrics</td>\n            <td>Regulatory headline risk creates an IV-expansion event; recovery pace correlated with whether monetisation metrics held in the quarters following the ruling</td>\n          </tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n\n      <p>[Note: episode drawdown magnitudes and recovery durations are approximate; verify against price history before citing numerically.]</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Mean-reversion implication:</strong> Prior episodes where Google experienced sharp drawdowns and recovered shared a common structural condition: user behaviour at the <strong>Search query layer remained intact</strong>. Ad-cycle recessions compressed revenue per query temporarily; Bing integration scared the multiple but did not move query-source share durably; DOJ rulings de-rated the distribution-moat premium but did not change where users began high-intent searches.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Structural caveat:</strong> These priors apply only when the query-origination behaviour is structurally stable. If Search query share migrates because users adopt AI assistants as their primary discovery layer — the interface-displacement failure mode — the historical mean-reversion priors do not apply. The recovery mechanism in prior episodes was mean-reverting ad economics, not mean-reverting user behaviour. Interface displacement would break the recovery mechanism itself: there is no historical precedent for Google recovering from durable query-origination share loss to a competing interface. The 2023 Bing episode is the closest analogue, and its resolution (Bing share gains marginalised) cannot be reliably extrapolated to a scenario where AI assistants are natively integrated at the OS, browser, and search-bar level at scale.</p>\n    </section>\n  </main>\n\n  <footer>Rendered from <code>playbooks/GOOG.md</code> on 2026-05-18 · regenerate to update.</footer>\n</div>\n\n<script>\n  const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('aside nav a'));\n  const targets = links.map(a => document.getElementById(a.getAttribute('href').slice(1))).filter(Boolean);\n  const byId = new Map(targets.map((el, i) => [el.id, links[i]]));\n  const io = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {\n    for (const e of entries) {\n      if (e.isIntersecting) {\n        links.forEach(a => a.classList.remove('active'));\n        byId.get(e.target.id)?.classList.add('active');\n      }\n    }\n  }, { rootMargin: '-30% 0px -60% 0px' });\n  targets.forEach(t => io.observe(t));\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"

Terminal margin anchors to low-20s; long-run earnings growth converges to low single digits.</dd>\n        <dt>base_narrative</dt><dd>Cost-temporary, monetisation-resilient: AI Overviews and AI Mode keep users inside Google surfaces; capex-to-revenue ratio mean-reverts post-2027 as model efficiency improves; Cloud (GCP) margin expands toward mid-20s. Terminal margin recovers to ~30% SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped FCF (Free Cash Flow) basis as the AI build-cycle normalises.</dd>\n        <dt>bull_narrative</dt><dd>AI amplifier — multiple independent upside vectors: (i) AI Mode + AI Overview monetise at parity-or-better RPM (Revenue Per Mille) vs. classical Search, sustaining revenue-per-query through the interface transition; (ii) GCP TPU + Vertex + Gemini-on-Cloud stack creates durable differentiation vs. AWS/Azure, expanding Cloud margins toward high-20s by FY2028; (iii) Waymo monetisation matures — multi-city fleet revenue and autonomous-driving licensing become a real P&amp;L (Profit and Loss) contributor; (iv) AI capex/revenue ratio declines post-FY2026 as model efficiency improves and capital-intensity normalises toward pre-AI levels; (v) DOJ and EU DMA (Digital Markets Act) remedies stay at conduct-rule margins, preserving default-placement economics in modified form; (vi) Gemini consumer adoption produces measurable first-place-I-ask share gain in high-intent commercial queries, reinforcing platform moat against AI-native alternatives.</dd>\n        <dt>failure_modes</dt><dd>\n          <ul>\n            <li>Interface displacement (structural): multi-quarter monotonic migration of commercial-intent queries to AI-native interfaces [interface layer]</li>\n            <li>Monetisation compression (structural): AI Overview / AI Mode rollout compresses revenue-per-search durably [monetisation layer]</li>\n            <li>Cost disruption (structural): AI capex/revenue ratio stays elevated beyond 2028 [cost layer]</li>\n            <li>Distribution remedy: DOJ remedies impair default-placement economics materially [ecosystem layer]</li>\n            <li>Cloud commoditisation: GCP margins fail to expand durably above mid-teens by 2027 [ecosystem layer]</li>\n            <li>Geo-regulatory contagion: EU DMA / India / other-jurisdiction remedies replicate US erosion [ecosystem layer]</li>\n          </ul>\n        </dd>\n      </dl>\n    </div>\n\n    <p><strong>Coverage status:</strong> ESTABLISHED · INCUMBENT<br>\n    <strong>Thesis in one line:</strong> AI-search-disruption debate + DOJ distribution-economics remedies + AI capex cost-permanence question — three structurally intertwined uncertainties that generic INCUMBENT/ESTABLISHED defaults cannot price.</p>\n    <hr>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"business-architecture\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">01</span><h2>Business Architecture</h2></header>\n\n      <h3 id=\"segment-mix\">Segment mix (approximate FY2025 basis)</h3>\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Segment</th><th>Revenue share</th><th>Growth trajectory</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>Google Search &amp; Other</td><td>~57%</td><td>Low-to-mid single digits; AI disruption is the structural risk</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>YouTube Ads</td><td>~11%</td><td>Mid-teens; subscription (YouTube Premium) adds a recurring layer</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Google Network (AdSense / AdMob / DV360)</td><td>~9%</td><td>Declining; programmatic ad-tech under AdTech regulatory scrutiny</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Google Cloud (GCP + Workspace)</td><td>~13%</td><td>~28–30% YoY; becoming the second material earnings contributor</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Google Other (Pixel, Play, Maps, subscriptions)</td><td>~5%</td><td>Mid-single digits; hardware margins thin</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Other Bets (Waymo, Verily, etc.)</td><td>~1%</td><td>R&amp;D-stage; not meaningful to near-term FCF</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n\n      <p><strong>Revenue driver mechanics:</strong></p>\n      <ol>\n        <li><strong>Search:</strong> Paid clicks × CPC (Cost Per Click). Absolute quarterly Search CPM (Cost Per Thousand Impressions) and click volumes are not disclosed by Alphabet (noted as OQ6 gap in the engagement-KPI map) — revenue-per-search trend is inferred from total Search &amp; Other revenue YoY, not directly observable. This limits the precision of monetisation-compression monitoring; the playbook does not attempt quarterly KPI tracking.</li>\n        <li><strong>YouTube:</strong> Primarily video ad auction (CPM-based); YouTube Premium subs add a lower-variance recurring line. Ad load and engagement trends are disclosed directionally but not with unit-economics granularity.</li>\n        <li><strong>Cloud:</strong> Committed GCP revenue backlog + Workspace seats. Backlog growth is disclosed quarterly; it is the leading indicator for Cloud revenue trajectory.</li>\n        <li><strong>Other Bets:</strong> Waymo is the only Other Bets asset with a plausible near-term monetisation path (robotaxi per-mile revenue, fleet licensing). Not material to DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) in the base case.</li>\n      </ol>\n\n      <h3 id=\"end-market-exposure\">End-market exposure</h3>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Digital advertising (~77% of revenue):</strong> Cyclical sensitivity to global ad-spend budgets; secular tail risk from AI-interface displacement.</li>\n        <li><strong>Enterprise cloud (~13% of revenue):</strong> GCP + Workspace; less cyclical; differentiated through Gemini integration.</li>\n        <li><strong>Hardware / consumer services (~5%):</strong> Pixel, Google One, Maps API — limited operating leverage.</li>\n      </ul>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"ai-investment-cycle-position\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">02</span><h2>AI Investment Cycle Position</h2></header>\n\n      <p>Alphabet spent ~$91B in FY2025 capex, ~70% AI-attributed per public guidance. This depresses TTM clean FCF margin and creates a two-sided uncertainty that is structurally different from a normal capex cycle trough: the normalisation path depends on <strong>which of two competing margin theses proves correct.</strong></p>\n\n      <p><strong>Path A — cost-temporary (base case):</strong><br>\n      AI model efficiency improves on hardware and software curves (inference cost-per-query falls as TPUs scale and model compression matures). Capex-as-share-of-revenue mean-reverts post-2027 as the build phase completes. Monetisation density per AI-assisted query holds near current levels or improves (AI Overviews maintain ad slots; AI Mode monetises at comparable RPM (Revenue Per Mille) to standard Search). Terminal margin recovers toward 30% SBC-stripped FCF.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Path B — cost-permanent (bear-case terminal margin thesis):</strong><br>\n      AI serving costs do not decay with scale at the rate Path A assumes — either because competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment, or because each AI query is structurally more compute-intensive than a traditional lookup. Simultaneously, AI-style answering reduces click-through rates, compressing ad density and CPC. Revenue growth decelerates while cost stays elevated. Terminal margin stabilises in the low-20s. This is the basis for <code>scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code>.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Base-case choice:</strong> The playbook picks Path A but does not assume the asymmetry away. The <code>terminal_margin</code> base of 30% reflects Path A prevailing. The bear <code>scenario_axes</code> captures Path B as a discrete scenario — not a symmetric delta from base — because interface displacement and cost-permanence cause joint compression of both growth and margin simultaneously, which a symmetric ±multiplier cannot represent.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Normalised-margin anchors:</strong> The <code>terminal_margin</code> base of 30% sits between two reference points. Reported TTM FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin is severely depressed by the AI build cycle — with ~$91B FY2025 capex, capex-blended group FCF margin is in the low-to-mid single digits (approximate; derived from disclosed capex and operating cash flows). On a normalised-capex, SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped basis — stripping the AI-attributed ~$64B capex increment above estimated pre-AI maintenance capex (~$25B) and SBC (~5–6% of revenue per disclosed annual figures) — clean FCF margin is inferred at approximately 22–27%: this is the distressed-floor reference point under Path A's recovery thesis. Search-segment-implied margin is structurally higher: Search &amp; Other at ~57% of revenue is Alphabet's highest-margin segment, with implied margins above 35% plausible given disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income of ~28–30% (approximate; GAAP segment FCF margins are not separately reported — treat these as order-of-magnitude anchors, not precise figures). The 30% base sits between the normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%) and the Search-segment ceiling (~35%+) — a defensible midpoint under Path A.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>AI-capex normalisation signal:</strong> The evidence-gating condition for Path A is a sustained decline in capex/revenue ratio after FY2026, visible across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that re-elevates above FY2025 levels by FY2028 would be evidence for Path B.</p>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"active-catalysts\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">03</span><h2>Active Catalysts</h2></header>\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Catalyst</th><th>Probability</th><th>IV impact</th><th>Direction</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>DOJ Search remedies finalised (default-payment restrictions, Chrome leverage, or divestiture ordered)</td><td>~35% material remedy by end-2027</td><td>−10–20%</td><td>Strongly negative — distribution economics impaired</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>AI Mode Search query-mix data disclosed showing CPC stability</td><td>~40% by end-2026</td><td>+5–10%</td><td>Positive — monetisation-compression bear case weakened</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>GCP margin print sustains above 15% for 2+ consecutive quarters</td><td>~55% by end-2027</td><td>+5–8%</td><td>Positive — Cloud-as-earnings-contributor thesis validated</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Gemini consumer adoption milestone (measurable first-place-I-ask share shift, third-party data)</td><td>~30% by end-2027</td><td>+3–7%</td><td>Positive — platform-lock thesis reinforced</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>AdTech structural separation ruling (forced unwind of ad-exchange vertical integration)</td><td>~25%</td><td>−8–15%</td><td>Negative — Network segment economics impaired</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>AI-native interface (ChatGPT / Perplexity / Claude) captures measurable commercial-intent query share (3rd-party panel data, sustained 2+ quarters)</td><td>~30% by end-2027</td><td>−15–25%</td><td>Strongly negative — interface-displacement thesis fires</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Waymo monetisation milestone (revenue-generating fleet in 3+ cities at scale)</td><td>~40% by end-2027</td><td>+2–5%</td><td>Modest positive — Other Bets optionality partially realised</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Capex/revenue ratio trajectory: FY2027 &lt; FY2026 for two consecutive years</td><td>~50%</td><td>+8–12%</td><td>Positive — Path A confirmed, terminal-margin re-rate</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"sell-side-disagreement-axes\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">04</span><h2>Sell-Side Disagreement Axes</h2></header>\n\n      <p>Organised by the <strong>4-layer AI-disruption taxonomy</strong> plus Cloud differentiation. Each axis names what distinguishes temporary noise from structural change.</p>\n\n      <h3 id=\"i-interface-disruption\">(i) Interface disruption</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Do AI assistants become the primary discovery and navigation layer, displacing Google Search as the first-place-I-ask interface for high-intent commercial queries?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> AI Overviews and AI Mode keep users inside Google surfaces for the queries that generate ad revenue; \"where do you start a purchase or research query\" surveys remain Google-dominant. Competitors capture curiosity and informational queries, not commercial-intent ones.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> AI-native interfaces (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, in-OS assistants, browser-native AI) capture meaningful share of commercial-intent queries — the queries that actually produce CPC revenue. Users who stop clicking to Google for high-intent searches stop generating ad impressions entirely.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> A single-quarter deceleration in Search revenue growth is noise — ad-cycle effects, macro, seasonality, and mix-shift within Search all produce this. Structural signal requires: monotonic commercial-intent query-share migration <strong>sustained across ≥3 quarters</strong>; \"first-place-I-ask\" data from third-party consumer panels showing a durable shift (not curiosity queries — specifically purchase-research, product-comparison, local-service-intent); revenue-per-search trend declining even in periods of macro-stable ad spend. All three together constitute structural signal; any one alone is insufficient.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"ii-monetisation-compression\">(ii) Monetisation compression</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Even at stable Search query share, does AI-style answering structurally compress revenue-per-search — via fewer ad slots per query, reduced click-through, or lower CPC?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> AI Overviews maintain or improve revenue-per-search through better ad-intent matching; users who get AI answers and then click on ads are higher-intent buyers; blended RPM (Revenue Per Mille) holds or expands.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> AI summaries satisfy the user's need without a click; ad slot count per query falls as above-the-fold content becomes AI-generated; CPC compresses as advertiser competition for fewer slots declines.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> Revenue-per-search trend over ≥2 quarters, filtered against macro ad-cycle movements by comparing to peer ad platforms (Meta, Snap, Pinterest) at the same periods. A revenue-per-search decline that tracks macro peers is cycle noise; one that diverges negatively from peers while the macro environment is stable is monetisation-compression signal. Absolute click volumes and CPM are not disclosed (OQ6 gap), so the observable proxy is total Search revenue growth rate relative to peer ad-platform growth rates.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"iii-cost-disruption\">(iii) Cost disruption</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Does AI inference cost remain structurally elevated, preventing margin recovery even if Search revenue holds?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> Inference cost-per-query declines on TPU hardware scaling and model-efficiency curves (distillation, quantisation, smaller purpose-built models); capex/revenue mean-reverts post-2027; operating leverage reasserts as fixed-cost build phase completes.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> AI serving cost is a permanent elevated line item — each AI query is computationally costlier than a keyword lookup by a structurally different order of magnitude; competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment to match quality; the cost-efficiency gains are real but are competed away in the form of better product rather than margin expansion.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> Capex/revenue ratio trend post-FY2026 across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that declines from FY2025 peak toward pre-AI levels (≤15% of revenue) is Path A signal. A ratio that stabilises above 18% of revenue through FY2028 is Path B signal. Gross-margin segmentation data (if and when disclosed at the Cloud or AI-products segment level) would be the most direct evidence but is not currently available.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"iv-ecosystem-and-distribution-displacement\">(iv) Ecosystem and distribution displacement</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Does regulatory and competitive erosion of Google's distribution advantages structurally weaken the default-placement economics that underpin Search market share?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> Distribution moats hold: Chrome browser default-search leverage continues, Apple default-search-engine payment (~$18–20B/year, market estimate) survives legal scrutiny in modified form, Android OEM agreements sustain Google's first-call position. Regulatory remedies stay at the margins (conduct rules, not structural separation).</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> DOJ remedies materially weaken default-placement economics — payments-for-default restricted or banned, Chrome divested or usage-gated, Android default-app leverage limited. Independent of which specific remedy is imposed: the structural question is whether Google's distribution advantages durably erode. An ecosystem-level erosion would move Search market share on a multi-year lag, not immediately — making it a slow-burn bear case, not a binary one.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> Actual remedies imposed (with material appeals exhausted, not just initial rulings); third-party measurement of default-search-engine market share in the 12–24 months post-remedy implementation. Court rulings that are appealed and do not result in operational changes are procedural noise; operational changes to the Chrome default or the Apple TAC (Traffic Acquisition Cost) payment are structural signal.</li>\n      </ul>\n\n      <h3 id=\"v-cloud-differentiation\">(v) Cloud differentiation</h3>\n      <p><strong>The question:</strong> Is GCP developing durable economic differentiation, or participating in a capital-intensive AI infrastructure cycle where margins normalise to mid-cycle hyperscaler economics?</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bull:</strong> TPU + Vertex AI + Gemini-on-Cloud create a stack-level differentiation that justifies sustained pricing power; enterprise customers building Gemini-powered workflows create switching-cost stickiness analogous to AWS-native application lock-in; GCP margin expands sustainably toward AWS/Azure levels (high-20s to low-30s).</li>\n        <li><strong>Bear:</strong> GCP participates in the AI capex cycle as a capacity provider, but without the enterprise-grade trust, developer ecosystem depth, or data-gravity advantages of AWS or Azure; margins normalise to mid-cycle hyperscaler economics (mid-teens); GCP is a strategic hedge for Alphabet but does not compensate for Search revenue risk.</li>\n        <li><strong>Noise vs. structural:</strong> GCP operating margin trajectory reported across ≥4 consecutive quarters at scale; pricing power signals from renewal rate commentary and enterprise customer-mix data (disclosed intermittently). GCP margins below 15% by FY2027 would weaken the base-case Cloud offset; margins expanding above 20% by FY2027 would strengthen the bull case.</li>\n      </ul>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"failure-modes\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">05</span><h2>Failure Modes</h2></header>\n\n      <p>These are the thesis-breaking scenarios that the DCF does not capture because they are discrete structural shifts rather than smooth-curve adjustments:</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Interface displacement (structural):</strong> Multi-quarter monotonic migration of commercial-intent queries to AI-native interfaces — invalidates the base revenue growth assumption. This is the failure mode that does not have a historical analogue in Alphabet's operating history: prior Search challengers (Bing, Yahoo relaunch) did not change user behaviour at the interface layer; AI assistants potentially do. [interface layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Monetisation compression (structural):</strong> AI Overview and AI Mode rollout compresses revenue-per-search durably; ad density falls as AI summaries occupy above-the-fold positions; CPC declines as advertiser competition for fewer slots decreases. This failure mode can coexist with stable query volumes — making it harder to detect via search share data alone. [monetisation layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Cost disruption (structural):</strong> AI capex/revenue ratio stays elevated beyond FY2028 with no margin recovery. In conjunction with monetisation compression, this produces joint revenue-and-margin pressure — the scenario captured by <code>scenario_axes.bear</code> compressing both <code>growth_ceiling</code> and <code>terminal_margin</code> simultaneously. [cost layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Distribution remedy:</strong> DOJ remedies impair default-placement economics materially. The specific form matters less than the functional outcome: if Google cannot pay for or mandate default Search placement in Chrome, Android, and Apple Safari, the structural query-share floor is removed. Independent of any single ruling's outcome — the structural impairment of distribution economics is the failure condition, not the legal calendar. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Cloud commoditisation:</strong> GCP margins fail to expand durably above mid-teens by FY2027. This eliminates the optionality embedded in the base case — the assumption that Cloud eventually becomes a material second earnings engine that partially offsets Search risk. If GCP remains a mid-margin business, the base case requires Search to sustain its current earnings contribution with no structural offset. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n        <li><strong>Geo-regulatory contagion:</strong> EU DMA, India CCI, and other-jurisdiction remedies replicate the distribution-economics erosion pattern outside the US market. The US DOJ case creates a precedent and negotiating template; a coordinated multi-jurisdiction wave of structural remedies could impair non-US revenue streams that are not currently in the bear-case model. [ecosystem layer]</li>\n      </ul>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"ticker-specific-overrides-rationale\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">06</span><h2>Ticker-Specific Overrides (Rationale)</h2></header>\n\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Value</th><th>Rationale</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>base_wacc</code></td>\n            <td>9.0%</td>\n            <td>US 10y ~4.5% + Beta ~1.05 × 5.5% ERP (Equity Risk Premium) ≈ 10.3%. Less ~1.0pp moat-durability discount (dominant Search economics + Cloud share gains remain intact today). Plus ~0.3pp regulatory premium (active DOJ remedies + AdTech + EU DMA + jurisdictional contagion risk). Sits at META parity (9.0%) rather than ASML monopoly level (8.5%) — Search durability is a live contested thesis, unlike ASML's EUV monopoly which has no credible near-term challenger.</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>growth_ceiling</code></td>\n            <td>13%</td>\n            <td>Fallback ceiling when <code>eps_growth_5y</code> is unavailable (current state per yfinance MCP). Below the generic 18% INCUMBENT default because: (a) $4.7T mega-cap mathematics constrain absolute growth, (b) Search (~57% of revenue) grows at ~5–7% and is the dominant segment, (c) Cloud (~13% of revenue) grows at ~28–30% but is not yet large enough to move the blended rate materially. Consensus <code>eps_growth_5y</code> takes precedence when populated; this override is the floor/ceiling for the fallback path only.</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>terminal_margin</code></td>\n            <td>30%</td>\n            <td>SBC-stripped FCF margin assuming Path A (cost-temporary) prevails. TTM clean margin is depressed by the AI build cycle. 30% sits between normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%, approximate; SBC-stripped, normalised-capex basis derived from disclosed segment data — not separately reported) and Search-segment ceiling (~35%+, approximate; inferred from disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income) — a defensible mid-range under the cost-temporary path. Path B (cost-permanent) downside is held discretely in <code>scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code>, not absorbed into the base value. Without <code>scenario_axes</code>, a 30% base-case terminal margin would be overconfident; with it, the base stays clean and the structural asymmetry is priced in the bear DCF.</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td><code>confidence_anchor</code></td>\n            <td>MEDIUM</td>\n            <td>The AI-disruption thesis spans four distinct structural questions (interface / monetisation / cost / ecosystem) that cannot be resolved from current financials. MCP data quality is adequate (4y FCF (Free Cash Flow), SBC, diluted shares present); LOW would be too pessimistic on data quality grounds. Structural-behavioural uncertainty is what caps confidence, not data availability. Below META's HIGH because META's central debate (regulatory) is discrete and binary; GOOG's central debate (interface displacement) is continuous, multi-modal, and decision-relevant in the base case, not just in tail scenarios.</td>\n          </tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n\n      <h3 id=\"scenario-axes-design-rationale\"><code>scenario_axes</code> design rationale</h3>\n      <p>Standard ±multiplier scenarios would produce symmetric bear/bull deltas from the base. GOOG's thesis is structurally asymmetric in a way that requires explicit overrides on both dimensions simultaneously:</p>\n      <ul>\n        <li><strong>Bear case:</strong> Interface displacement causes <strong>joint</strong> compression of growth ceiling (query share migrates) and terminal margin (monetisation compresses + costs stay elevated). A symmetric −5pp terminal-margin delta off 30% (i.e., 25%) understates the joint structural-break shape. <code>bear.growth_ceiling: 0.04</code> anchors below the symmetric multiplier because the bear case is not a cycle trough — it is an interface-layer shift where EPS growth converges toward low single digits. <code>bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code> sits below the TTM-clean FCF margin to reflect the joint structural break, not a recoverable cycle compression.</li>\n        <li><strong>Bull case:</strong> The bull thesis is monetisation-density improvement + Cloud acceleration. <code>bull.growth_ceiling: 0.18</code> matches the upper bound of pre-AI-discount consensus and allows the bull-case DCF to capture upside without being artificially compressed by the 13% fallback. <code>bull.terminal_margin: 0.32</code> is a modest above-base anchor for the scenario where Path A delivers cleanly and AI Overviews monetise at parity to current Search.</li>\n      </ul>\n      <p>Unspecified scenario fields fall back to standard ±multiplier per the loader spec.</p>\n    </section>\n\n    <section class=\"s\" id=\"historical-reset-and-recover-priors\">\n      <header><span class=\"ix\">07</span><h2>Historical Reset-and-Recover Priors</h2></header>\n\n      <table>\n        <thead><tr><th>Episode</th><th>Drawdown (approx)</th><th>Catalyst</th><th>Recovery</th><th>Lesson</th></tr></thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr>\n            <td>2022 ad recession + iOS privacy reset</td>\n            <td>~−45% peak-to-trough</td>\n            <td>Macro ad-spend contraction; Apple ATT (App Tracking Transparency) headwinds to ad-targeting quality</td>\n            <td>~12 months; recovery on ad-market rebound and YouTube brand-advertiser return</td>\n            <td>Cyclical ad recessions recover on macro normalisation; the underlying monetisation mechanics remained intact throughout</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td>2023 Bing + ChatGPT integration scare</td>\n            <td>~−15% drawdown</td>\n            <td>Microsoft integrated GPT-4 into Bing; sell-side concern about Search displacement</td>\n            <td>~6 months; recovered as Bing share gains remained marginal and Google announced Bard/Gemini roadmap</td>\n            <td>A credible competitive interface challenge caused a multiple de-rate, but was not sufficient to structurally impair query economics at the monetisation layer</td>\n          </tr>\n          <tr>\n            <td>2024–2025 DOJ verdict + AI-Mode launch uncertainty</td>\n            <td>~−20–25% drawdown (approximate)</td>\n            <td>DOJ liability finding in Search distribution case; uncertainty around AI Mode cannibalising Search RPM (Revenue Per Mille)</td>\n            <td>Partial recovery as AI Overviews maintained revenue-per-search in initial disclosed metrics</td>\n            <td>Regulatory headline risk creates an IV-expansion event; recovery pace correlated with whether monetisation metrics held in the quarters following the ruling</td>\n          </tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n\n      <p>[Note: episode drawdown magnitudes and recovery durations are approximate; verify against price history before citing numerically.]</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Mean-reversion implication:</strong> Prior episodes where Google experienced sharp drawdowns and recovered shared a common structural condition: user behaviour at the <strong>Search query layer remained intact</strong>. Ad-cycle recessions compressed revenue per query temporarily; Bing integration scared the multiple but did not move query-source share durably; DOJ rulings de-rated the distribution-moat premium but did not change where users began high-intent searches.</p>\n\n      <p><strong>Structural caveat:</strong> These priors apply only when the query-origination behaviour is structurally stable. If Search query share migrates because users adopt AI assistants as their primary discovery layer — the interface-displacement failure mode — the historical mean-reversion priors do not apply. The recovery mechanism in prior episodes was mean-reverting ad economics, not mean-reverting user behaviour. Interface displacement would break the recovery mechanism itself: there is no historical precedent for Google recovering from durable query-origination share loss to a competing interface. The 2023 Bing episode is the closest analogue, and its resolution (Bing share gains marginalised) cannot be reliably extrapolated to a scenario where AI assistants are natively integrated at the OS, browser, and search-bar level at scale.</p>\n    </section>\n  </main>\n\n  <footer>Rendered from <code>playbooks/GOOG.md</code> on 2026-05-18 · regenerate to update.</footer>\n</div>\n\n<script>\n  const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('aside nav a'));\n  const targets = links.map(a => document.getElementById(a.getAttribute('href').slice(1))).filter(Boolean);\n  const byId = new Map(targets.map((el, i) => [el.id, links[i]]));\n  const io = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {\n    for (const e of entries) {\n      if (e.isIntersecting) {\n        links.forEach(a => a.classList.remove('active'));\n        byId.get(e.target.id)?.classList.add('active');\n      }\n    }\n  }, { rootMargin: '-30% 0px -60% 0px' });\n  targets.forEach(t => io.observe(t));\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"

25	# ASML Playbook
26	
27	**Coverage status:** ESTABLISHED · INFRASTRUCTURE  
28	**Thesis in one line:** EUV monopoly + High-NA ramp + China export-control overhang, with the semiconductor capex cycle as the dominant input.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## 1. Business Architecture
33	
34	### Segment mix (approximate FY2025 basis)
35	
36	| Segment | Revenue share | Growth trajectory |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| EUV systems (standard + High-NA) | ~50% | Cycle-dependent; High-NA ramp adds a step-up from 2026 |
39	| Advanced DUV (immersion) | ~25% | Mature; sensitive to logic node digestion pace |
40	| Mature DUV (dry, KrF, i-line) | ~10% | Stable; exposed to auto / industrial / mature-node capex |
41	| Installed Base Management (IBM) — services + upgrades | ~15% | Most defensive; ~25% of revenue; less cyclical than new tool orders |
42	
43	IBM (Installed Base Management) is the earnings-floor segment: service contracts and upgrades on the ~4,000-tool installed base continue regardless of new-system order cycles. It is the component most vulnerable to a China-service-rule tightening scenario (see Failure Modes).
44	
45	### Key revenue drivers
46	
47	1. **EUV unit shipments** — the volume metric for leading-edge logic. Consensus expects a step-up to ~90–100 units/year by 2027 from ~50–60 in 2024; below-60 for two consecutive years is a bearish inflection signal.
48	2. **High-NA EUV ramp** — ASP (Average Selling Price) per High-NA tool is ~€350M vs ~€200M for standard EUV. Even 5 additional High-NA units/year moves blended ASP materially. First customer is TSMC; Intel and Samsung are expected second/third.
49	3. **China revenue share** — ranged 20–49% of system revenue (2022–2023 peak) before export-control restrictions; tracking ~15–20% under current rules. Further rule tightening is the bear-case revenue risk; stabilisation at current levels is the base case.
50	4. **IBM attach rate** — services revenue as % of cumulative installed base value. Rising attach rate signals customer utilisation and confidence; falling attach rate (e.g., from China service restrictions) is the canary in the earnings-floor thesis.
51	
52	### End-market exposure
53	
54	- **Leading-edge logic (HPC/AI + smartphones):** TSMC, Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry — drive EUV and High-NA demand
55	- **Memory (DRAM + NAND):** SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung Memory — drive EUV-for-DRAM and advanced-patterning demand
56	- **Mature logic / specialty:** auto, industrial, IoT via mature DUV (less cyclically exposed but not immune)
57	
58	Customer concentration: TSMC + Samsung + Intel represent the dominant share of EUV system revenue. [TODO: verify exact top-3/top-5 % against latest ASML 20-F / annual report risk-factor disclosure — do not cite a specific number without verification]

60	---
61	
62	## 2. Capex-Cycle Position
63	
64	ASML is in a **cycle-trough / inflection** phase as of mid-2026. The 2024–2025 digestion period (customers pausing orders after COVID-era over-ordering of DUV tools) is expected to trough in 2026, with re-acceleration in 2027–2029 on two overlapping drivers:
65	
66	1. **AI-driven advanced-node demand:** TSMC N2/N2P, Samsung 2GAP, Intel 18A ramps require sustained EUV intensity. Hyperscaler custom-silicon fabs (Google, Meta, Amazon) are incremental new demand on top of smartphone-driven baseline.
67	2. **High-NA volume ramp:** First High-NA tools are being qualified at TSMC Arizona and Intel Ohio. If High-NA economics validate (cost-per-wafer clears vs multi-patterning DUV), the step-up in ASP per unit creates a revenue tailwind independent of unit-volume growth.
68	
69	**Normalised-margin thesis:** The `terminal_margin` override of 30% assumes High-NA reaches mature unit economics, customer utilisation normalises post-trough, and customer-prepayment working-capital swings dampen over a full cycle. TTM clean FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin (~24%) is trough-distorted by both the demand digestion period and ramp-related investment; anchoring the DCF on TTM understates steady-state. The 30% base sits between TTM clean FCF (~24%) and TTM earnings margin (~35%, implied by P/E 49.5 / P/S 17.18) — a defensible midpoint.
70	
71	**Bear case:** If High-NA economics fail to clear at scale OR if the semi cycle air-pocket is deeper than expected, utilisation stays weak and terminal margin compresses to TTM-clean levels. This is exactly what `scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.24` captures — it anchors the bear terminal margin at the observed trough rather than at a symmetric ±delta from base.
72
