## P21 — Bull / Bear / Noise-vs-Structural axis grid *(promotion of ASML custom CSS)*

**Detect.** H2 matches `/sell[- ]side disagreement|disagreement axes|the question(s)? sell[- ]side is having/i` AND inside the section, two-or-more H3s each followed by a structured block where the **first** non-empty paragraph after the H3 is bolded and contains `the question` (case-insensitive), AND the subsequent body contains bolded labels matching `Bull:`, `Bear:`, and `Noise vs.? structural:` (in any order). Detection is per-axis-H3: each H3 that meets the per-axis conditions becomes a card; H3s in the same section that don't meet the conditions fall through to prose.

**Markdown shape.** Matches both GOOG.md (`### (i) Interface disruption` … `**The question:** …` … `- **Bull:** …` `- **Bear:** …` `- **Noise vs. structural:** …`) and ASML.md (`### 1. Capex-cycle trough timing` etc.) as-written. Zero markdown changes.

**HTML.** Three regions: a question banner (full-width header), then a two-column Bull/Bear pair, then a full-width NVS panel beneath. This is the same shape ASML.html currently produces:

```html
<article class="p-axis-card" id="axis-1">
  <header class="p-axis-head">
    <h3>1. Capex-cycle trough timing</h3>
    <p class="p-axis-q">Does the semiconductor capex cycle trough in H2 2026…?</p>
  </header>
  <div class="p-axis-body">
    <div class="p-axis-views">
      <div class="p-axis-view p-axis-bull">
        <span class="p-axis-label">Bull</span>
        TSMC has sustained its 2025 and 2026 capex guidance…
      </div>
      <div class="p-axis-view p-axis-bear">
        <span class="p-axis-label">Bear</span>
        Memory oversupply (DRAM/NAND inventory digestion) is slower-than-consensus…
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="p-axis-nvs">
      <span class="p-axis-label">Noise vs. structural</span>
      A single quarter of order intake recovery or SEMI book-to-bill above 1.0 is noise…
    </div>
  </div>
</article>
```

**CSS** (port of `.axis-card` / `.bull-view` / `.bear-view` / `.nvs` from ASML.html lines 115–128, re-keyed and re-coloured to shell tokens):

```css
.p-axis-card { border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 10px;
  margin: 18px 0; overflow: hidden; background: var(--surface); }
.p-axis-head { padding: 14px 18px; background: var(--rule-soft);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
.p-axis-head h3 { margin: 0 0 4px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--fg); scroll-margin-top: 20px; }
.p-axis-q { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--muted); font-style: italic; }
.p-axis-body { padding: 16px 18px; }
.p-axis-views { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
.p-axis-view { border-radius: 8px; padding: 14px 16px;
  font-size: 14.5px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--fg); }
.p-axis-bull { background: var(--ok-soft); border: 1px solid var(--ok); }
.p-axis-bear { background: var(--danger-soft); border: 1px solid var(--danger); }
.p-axis-nvs  { background: var(--rule-soft); border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14.5px; line-height: 1.6;
  color: var(--fg-soft); }
.p-axis-label { display: block; font: 700 11px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; margin-bottom: 6px; }
.p-axis-bull .p-axis-label { color: var(--ok); }
.p-axis-bear .p-axis-label { color: var(--danger); }
.p-axis-nvs  .p-axis-label { color: var(--muted); }
@media (max-width: 720px) { .p-axis-views { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
```

The migration replaces ASML.html's hardcoded `#f0fdf4 / #bbf7d0` (bull) and `#fff5f5 / #fecaca` (bear) with the shell's `--ok-soft / --ok` and `--danger-soft / --danger` tokens — the dark-mode appearance comes for free.

**Accessibility.** `<article>` per axis; H3 keeps the document outline; question is a `<p>` not a heading so it doesn't pollute TOC; label `<span>`s carry text (`Bull`, `Bear`, `Noise vs. structural`) — colour is supplemental.

**Migration note (ASML.html → P21 markdown).** The ASML.html hand-authored `<div class="axis-card">…</div>` blocks (lines 351–467) can be deleted entirely; the markdown source already carries the canonical form. The renderer produces the new `p-axis-card` markup automatically. No new markdown is required.

**When to use.** Playbook §4. Any future ticker following the `### N. Axis name` / `**The question:**` / `**Bull:**` / `**Bear:**` / `**Noise vs. structural:**` convention.
**When not to use.** Sections that look like sell-side disagreement but only carry Bull/Bear bullets without `The question:` framing — fall through to prose. The `The question:` paragraph is the key trigger that distinguishes "real axis" from "generic bull/bear summary."

**Verification.** Each axis renders as one card with the three regions; Bull is green-tinted, Bear is red-tinted, NVS is neutral; dark mode flips backgrounds; mobile collapses Bull/Bear into a single column.

## P22 — Layer-tagged failure-mode cards *(promotion of ASML custom CSS)*

**Detect.** H2 matches `/failure modes?|thesis[- ]breaking|structural failure/i` AND the body's primary content is a bullet list (allowing optional intro `<p>` above) where **at least 50% of the bullets** end with a bracketed `[xxx layer]` tag (case-insensitive, allowing `[FX layer]`, `[regulatory layer]`, `[accounting layer]`, etc.). The 50% threshold accommodates partial-migration playbooks; if no bullets have tags, fall through to prose. The renderer extracts the tag from each bullet and the bullet body before it, plus the leading `**bold lead-in:**` if present.

**Markdown shape.** Matches GOOG.md lines 148–158 and ASML.md lines 162–172 as-written (each bullet ends with `[interface layer]`, `[demand layer]`, etc.). Zero markdown changes.

**Layer palette (fixed across all playbooks).** The renderer maps each layer literal to a token pair; the table below is the authoritative mapping and must be reproduced verbatim in the catalogue entry:

| Layer literal | Class | Background token | Foreground token |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interface` | `p-fm-tag-interface` | `--accent-soft` | `--accent` |
| `monetisation` / `monetization` | `p-fm-tag-monetisation` | `--info-soft` | `--info` |
| `cost` | `p-fm-tag-cost` | `--warn-soft` | `--warn` |
| `ecosystem` | `p-fm-tag-ecosystem` | `--info-soft` | `--info` |
| `demand` | `p-fm-tag-demand` | `--danger-soft` | `--danger` |
| `regulatory` | `p-fm-tag-regulatory` | `--warn-soft` | `--warn` |
| `technology` | `p-fm-tag-technology` | `--accent-soft` | `--accent` |
| `accounting` | `p-fm-tag-accounting` | `--rule-soft` | `--muted` |
| `FX` | `p-fm-tag-fx` | `--info-soft` | `--info` |

Unknown layers (a future playbook might add `[supply layer]` or `[geo layer]`) fall to a default `p-fm-tag-other` using `--rule-soft / --muted`.

**HTML.** Optional legend strip above (auto-generated from the set of layers actually present in the section), then one card per bullet:

```html
<div class="p-fm-section">
  <div class="p-fm-legend" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="p-fm-tag p-fm-tag-demand">demand</span>
    <span class="p-fm-tag p-fm-tag-regulatory">regulatory</span>
    <span class="p-fm-tag p-fm-tag-technology">technology</span>
    <span class="p-fm-tag p-fm-tag-accounting">accounting</span>
    <span class="p-fm-tag p-fm-tag-fx">FX</span>
  </div>
  <ul class="p-fm-list">
    <li class="p-fm-card">
      <span class="p-fm-tag p-fm-tag-demand">demand</span>
      <div class="p-fm-body">
        <strong>Customer concentration shock:</strong> TSMC + Samsung + Intel
        represent the dominant share of EUV system revenue…
      </div>
    </li>
    <!-- one <li> per failure mode -->
  </ul>
</div>
```

The legend is `aria-hidden` because each card already carries its tag — duplicating the tag set in the accessibility tree would be noise.

**CSS** (port of `.fm` / `.fm-tag` from ASML.html lines 130–137, re-keyed and palette-bound to shell tokens):

```css
.p-fm-section { margin: 18px 0; }
.p-fm-legend { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 14px; }
.p-fm-list { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
.p-fm-card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr;
  gap: 14px; align-items: start; padding: 14px 18px;
  background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule);
  border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14.5px; line-height: 1.6; }
.p-fm-body { color: var(--fg-soft); }
.p-fm-body strong { color: var(--fg); }
.p-fm-tag { font: 700 10.5px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 5px 10px;
  border-radius: 4px; white-space: nowrap; align-self: start; margin-top: 2px; }
.p-fm-tag-interface     { background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent); }
.p-fm-tag-monetisation,
.p-fm-tag-monetization  { background: var(--info-soft);   color: var(--info); }
.p-fm-tag-cost          { background: var(--warn-soft);   color: var(--warn); }
.p-fm-tag-ecosystem     { background: var(--info-soft);   color: var(--info); }
.p-fm-tag-demand        { background: var(--danger-soft); color: var(--danger); }
.p-fm-tag-regulatory    { background: var(--warn-soft);   color: var(--warn); }
.p-fm-tag-technology    { background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent); }
.p-fm-tag-accounting,
.p-fm-tag-other         { background: var(--rule-soft);   color: var(--muted); }
.p-fm-tag-fx            { background: var(--info-soft);   color: var(--info); }
```

**Accessibility.** `<ul>` semantics preserved; tag `<span>` carries the layer text; the card grid is purely visual. Legend is `aria-hidden`; the tags inside each card carry the meaning for screen readers.

**Precedence.** P22 ranks above P17 inside playbook documents. P17 detects a table with `Risk | Sev | Mitigation` headers; P22 detects bullets with `[xxx layer]` tags. The two never co-trigger in practice because playbook failure-mode sections are always bullets, never tables.

**Migration note (ASML.html → P22 markdown).** The ASML.html `<div class="fm-list">…</div>` block (lines 472–497) can be deleted entirely; the markdown source already carries the canonical form. The renderer's tag-extraction regex (`/\[([a-zA-Z]+) layer\]\s*$/`) reads from the bullet's trailing text. No new markdown is required.

**When to use.** Playbook §5. Any future ticker bullet-list where modes end with `[xxx layer]` tags.
**When not to use.** Failure-mode sections rendered as a `<table>` — that goes to P17. Bullets without layer tags — fall through to prose.

**Verification.** Legend shows the unique set of layers present; each card carries its tag; colours match the palette table above; unknown layers fall to the `-other` muted style; dark mode preserves all tag contrasts (the soft companions all have dark-mode versions).

---

## P23 — Scenario-axes shape plot *(reads from frontmatter, not body)*

**Detect.** This pattern is unusual: it does not detect on body markdown shape. Instead, it activates whenever the renderer's frontmatter parser (P9) produces a `scenario_axes` field with at least one of `bear.{growth_ceiling, terminal_margin}` or `bull.{growth_ceiling, terminal_margin}` populated. The plot lifts into the body once, immediately under the §6 H2 (which is matched separately by header text `/overrides|rationale/i`). If §6 isn't present, the plot lifts immediately before §1.

**Why this special-case.** `scenario_axes` is data, not prose. It exists to describe the asymmetric shape of bear / base / bull on a (growth × margin) plane. Both GOOG and ASML explain this shape verbally in their §6 rationale prose. A small SVG plot replaces the need to read three paragraphs to picture three points.

**Data extraction from frontmatter.** Frontmatter fields used:

```yaml
growth_ceiling: 0.13                # base
terminal_margin: 0.30               # base
scenario_axes:
  bear:
    growth_ceiling: 0.04            # bear override (else fall back to base × 0.6)
    terminal_margin: 0.22           # bear override (else fall back to base − 5pp)
  bull:
    growth_ceiling: 0.18            # bull override (else fall back to base × 1.3)
    terminal_margin: 0.32           # bull override (else fall back to base + 3pp)
```

When ASML's frontmatter omits `bear.growth_ceiling` and `bull.terminal_margin`, the renderer uses the documented `±multiplier` fallback (which is what the DCF loader itself uses) so the plot visualises the same shape the DCF actually computes. The fallback formulas should be added to the catalogue entry verbatim so they stay stable.

**HTML.**

```html
<figure class="p-scenshape">
  <figcaption class="p-scenshape-cap">Scenario shape · growth ceiling × terminal margin</figcaption>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 320 240" role="img"
       aria-label="Bear: growth 4%, margin 22%. Base: growth 13%, margin 30%. Bull: growth 18%, margin 32%.">
    <!-- gridlines -->
    <g class="p-scenshape-grid">
      <line x1="40" y1="20"  x2="40"  y2="200"/>
      <line x1="40" y1="200" x2="300" y2="200"/>
      <line x1="40" y1="110" x2="300" y2="110" stroke-dasharray="2 3"/>
      <line x1="170" y1="20" x2="170" y2="200" stroke-dasharray="2 3"/>
    </g>
    <!-- axis labels -->
    <text x="170" y="230" text-anchor="middle" class="p-scenshape-axis">growth ceiling →</text>
    <text x="20" y="110" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90,20,110)" class="p-scenshape-axis">terminal margin →</text>
    <!-- polygon connecting bear → base → bull -->
    <polygon points="65,180 200,80 260,60"
             fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <!-- three points + labels -->
    <circle cx="65"  cy="180" r="6" fill="var(--danger)"/>
    <text   x="65"   y="200" text-anchor="middle" class="p-scenshape-pt">Bear (4%, 22%)</text>
    <circle cx="200" cy="80"  r="6" fill="var(--accent)"/>
    <text   x="200"  y="68"  text-anchor="middle" class="p-scenshape-pt">Base (13%, 30%)</text>
    <circle cx="260" cy="60"  r="6" fill="var(--ok)"/>
    <text   x="260"  y="48"  text-anchor="middle" class="p-scenshape-pt">Bull (18%, 32%)</text>
  </svg>
</figure>
```

The plot uses fixed-range axes: growth `0%–25%` (x-axis spans `40–300 px`), terminal margin `15%–40%` (y-axis spans `200–20 px`). These ranges cover every coverage ticker — META has growth_ceiling up to ~22% in bull, ASML margins down to 24% in bear. The renderer normalises each point's coordinates with the formula in the catalogue entry. The `<polygon>` connects the three points in canonical order (bear → base → bull) so the shape's asymmetry — symmetric ±delta = isoceles triangle on the diagonal; structural-break shape = elongated or skewed triangle — is visible at a glance.

**CSS.**

```css

  border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 10px;
  padding: 20px 22px; max-width: 480px; }

```

**Accessibility.** `role="img"` with full `aria-label` describing all three scenario points. The figure is supplementary; the source `scenario_axes` rationale prose (already in §6 §6 body) carries the canonical explanation.

**When to use.** Any playbook frontmatter with a `scenario_axes:` block. Both GOOG and ASML qualify today; META currently does not have one populated but should activate once one is added.
**When not to use.** Frontmatter without `scenario_axes`. No fallback shape — the plot's value comes from comparing bear/base/bull positions.

**Verification.** Three dots positioned consistent with the values in frontmatter; bear dot is bottom-left of base, bull dot is top-right (in the typical case); polygon fill is accent-soft; the label `aria-label` reads the three numeric pairs.

## P24 — Reset-and-recover timeline

**Detect.** H2 matches `/historical reset|reset[- ]and[- ]recover|recovery prior|historical prior/i` AND a markdown table whose header row contains all three of (case-insensitive): `episode`, `drawdown`, `recovery`. Optional further columns (`catalyst`, `lesson`) are preserved as the row's caption text.

**Choice: scatter plot over horizontal time-bar.** A horizontal time-bar requires precise start/end dates per episode; the source data is `~−45% peak-to-trough` and `~12 months recovery` — magnitude and duration, not calendar bounds. A scatter on `(recovery duration, drawdown magnitude)` reads as "how deep × how long" — exactly the dimensions the analyst is communicating. The original table sits below as the canonical legend.

**Data extraction.** From each row, the renderer parses:
- `drawdown_pct = abs(int from /~?−?\d+/)` matched in the Drawdown cell, taking the upper end of any range (`−20–25%` → 25);
- `recovery_months = int from /~?\d+/` matched in the Recovery cell (`~14 months` → 14, `Partial recovery` → fallback 18 to bias toward "longer");
- `episode = trimmed Episode cell`.

**Markdown shape.** Matches GOOG.md §7 (3 rows) and ASML.md §7 (3 rows) as-written. Zero markdown changes.

## Slicing recommendation — three implementation slices

The slicing strategy puts the lowest-risk migrations first so the renderer infrastructure is exercised under known-correct conditions before any new visual logic ships.

**Slice 1 — promotions only (P21 + P22).** Lift the ASML inline CSS into the catalogue and re-key class names. No new visual logic; the rendering tree is what ASML.html already produces, just driven from markdown instead of hand-authored HTML. Token-binding (`#f0fdf4 → var(--ok-soft)`, `#fee2e2 → var(--danger-soft)`, etc.) means dark mode starts working everywhere it didn't before. GOOG.html immediately gains both sections. The verification surface is two playbooks × two sections = four cases; each is visually comparable to the existing ASML.html snapshot. Risk: low. Dependencies: needs the renderer to be able to detect H3 axis cards and bullet-with-trailing-tag — both straightforward regex.

**Slice 2 — table-driven inline charts (P18 + P20 + P24).** Three patterns that all extract data from existing markdown tables and decorate the table with inline SVG. Common implementation primitive: a "numeric-cell parser" that converts cells like `~35%`, `−10–20%`, `~14 months` into numeric values. Build the parser once, then each pattern is ~30 lines of SVG-generation. No detection ambiguity: each pattern has a unique header-column signature. Verification surface: six chart renderings (three patterns × two playbooks). Risk: low-medium — the parser needs care on ranges and approximations. Dependencies: Slice 1 confirms the renderer's pattern hook is reliable.

**Slice 3 — narrative + frontmatter patterns (P19 + P23).** P19 has the strictest detection rule of any pattern in the catalogue (three concurrent conditions) and consumes free-form paragraph prose — it's the highest-risk pattern in the set. P23 reads from frontmatter, which means it depends on the P9 parser producing a `scenario_axes` shape correctly. Both patterns are also the most editorial — small detection misses can mean a chart never appears, which is a quality-of-output issue more than a correctness bug. Risk: medium. Dependencies: Slice 2 builds confidence in inline-SVG rendering and the renderer's chart pipeline.

This three-slice order means every commit lands a coherent set of patterns and the rendered playbook gets visibly richer at each step. No slice introduces a regression on the patterns that landed previously because all P18–P24 detection conditions are mutually disjoint.

## Dark-mode and print considerations

The skeleton already swaps every token via `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` (see html-skeleton.md lines 70–84). All P18–P24 CSS uses **only** these tokens — no hardcoded hex values — so dark mode works without per-pattern overrides. Two pattern-specific notes:

- **SVG background assumption.** P18, P23, and P24 each wrap their SVG in a parent element with `background: var(--surface)` so the chart sits on the right canvas regardless of mode. P14 (existing diagram pattern) already follows this convention. Do not omit the wrapper — an unwrapped SVG inherits `var(--bg)` from `<main>` but loses the framing.
- **Label text fill on coloured slices.** P18's segment-bar labels use `fill: var(--bg)` (line 8 of its CSS) so they invert in dark mode — light text on a dark slice fill, dark text on a light slice fill. This is the only fill where the visual contrast comes from inverting against the slice colour rather than against the page background.

**Print considerations.** The skeleton hides `aside` and expands `main` (lines 187–191). Pattern CSS does not need print rules of its own — every pattern's HTML degrades gracefully in print because (a) no pattern relies on hover state for legibility, (b) every SVG is inline and prints with the page, (c) every chart has a co-located source `<table>` or paragraph that carries the canonical data for greyscale prints where colour distinctions weaken. The one minor consideration: P18's six-token slice cycle (`accent, info, warn, ok, danger, muted`) has distinct luminance values in greyscale, so the bar is still readable in B&W; if a future playbook has >6 segments, the bar should fall through to prose (already specified in P18's "when not to use").

Slice labels render only on slices ≥8%; the source table below carries the full legend.\n- **Why bar, not donut:** Donuts hide the long tail and don't print well. The bar reads left-to-right, prints in B&W, and the table remains the canonical data source.\n- **Markdown change:** None. Both GOOG.md §1 and ASML.md §1 already match.\n\n### P19 — Margin position-band strip (§2)\n\n- **Detect (strict, three concurrent conditions):** H2 matching `/(capex|AI investment) cycle|cycle position|normalised margin/i` AND a paragraph containing all of (a) a keyword like `floor / ceiling / base / anchor / sits between`, (b) at least two `%` anchors, (c) within 250 characters of each other.\n- **Render:** Horizontal range strip with gradient track (`--danger-soft → --warn-soft → --ok-soft`), endpoint labels for floor and ceiling, marker tick at the base anchor. Tick position computed from `(base − low) / (high − low)`.\n- **Why strict trigger:** DCF prose is dense with `%` figures that aren't position anchors. Falling through to prose is the correct default; only render the strip when the anchor framing is unambiguous.\n- **Markdown change:** None. GOOG.md §2 (\"Normalised-margin anchors\") and ASML.md §2 (\"Normalised-margin thesis\") both match.\n\n### P20 — Catalyst probability × IV-impact mini-bars (§3)\n\n- **Detect:** H2 matching `/catalysts?/i` AND a table with headers matching `Catalyst` + `Probability` + `IV impact`.\n- **Render:** The existing markdown table augmented with two extra cells per row — a blue probability bar and a green/red IV-impact bar (width = midpoint of any range like `−10–20%`, capped at 30% for visual normalisation). Direction column becomes a pill (`--ok-soft / --ok` for positive, `--danger-soft / --danger` for negative, `--warn-soft / --warn` for mixed).\n- **Why inline mini-bars, not scatter:** 8 catalyst points on a scatter lose label legibility; mini-bars preserve identity and table-scan order.\n- **Markdown change:** None. Both §3 tables match.\n\n### P21 — Bull / Bear / Noise-vs-Structural axis grid (§4) — **promotion of existing ASML CSS**\n\n- **Detect:** H2 matching `/sell[- ]side disagreement|disagreement axes/i` AND per-axis H3s where each has a `**The question:**` line followed by `**Bull:**` / `**Bear:**` / `**Noise vs. structural:**` blocks.\n- **Render:** Per-axis card: full-width question banner, two-column Bull/Bear pair (green-soft / red-soft tints), full-width NVS panel beneath (neutral tint). Mobile collapses to single column.\n- **Migration from ASML.html:** Re-key the existing `.axis-card / .bull-block / .bear-block / .nvs` classes to `.p-axis-card / .p-axis-bull / .p-axis-bear / .p-axis-nvs`; swap hardcoded hexes for `--ok-soft / --ok` (bull) and `--danger-soft / --danger` (bear). The hand-authored `<div class=\"axis-card\">` blocks in ASML.html lines 351–467 disappear — replaced by pattern-driven markup.\n- **Markdown change:** None. Both playbooks already use the canonical shape.\n\n### P22 — Layer-tagged failure-mode cards (§5) — **promotion of existing ASML CSS**\n\n- **Detect:** H2 matching `/failure modes?/i` AND a bullet list where ≥50% of items end with `[xxx layer]` tags.\n- **Render:** Per-mode card with a left-positioned coloured chip carrying the layer label. Auto-generated legend strip above (`aria-hidden`, since each card carries its own tag for screen readers). Fixed palette mapping nine known layers (`interface`, `monetisation`, `cost`, `ecosystem`, `demand`, `regulatory`, `technology`, `accounting`, `FX`) to specific token pairs; unknown layers fall to a muted `-other` style.\n- **Migration from ASML.html:** Re-key existing `.fm / .fm-tag` classes to `.p-fm-card / .p-fm-tag`; bind tag-specific colours to the layer palette. ASML.html's `<div class=\"fm-list\">…</div>` block (lines 472–497) is deleted.\n- **Markdown change:** None. All ASML and GOOG failure-mode bullets already end with `[xxx layer]`.\n\n### P23 — Scenario-axes shape plot (§6) — **reads from frontmatter, not body**\n\n- **Detect:** P9 frontmatter parser produces a `scenario_axes` field with bear/bull deltas on `growth_ceiling` and/or `terminal_margin`. The plot lifts into the body immediately under the §6 H2 (matched by `/overrides|rationale/i`).\n- **Render:** Small inline SVG plot — x-axis = growth ceiling (0–25%), y-axis = terminal margin (15–40%), three points (bear / base / bull) connected by a polygon (`fill: --accent-soft`). Reads the shape's asymmetry at a glance: structural-break shape (asymmetric polygon) vs symmetric ±delta shape (isoceles triangle).\n- **Fallback formulas:** When bear/bull overrides are absent, the renderer uses the same `±multiplier` formulas the DCF loader uses (documented in the catalogue entry verbatim so they don't drift).\n- **Markdown change:** None. Both playbooks' frontmatter already populates `scenario_axes`.\n\n### P24 — Reset-and-recover scatter (§7)\n\n- **Detect:** H2 matching `/historical reset|reset[- ]and[- ]recover|recovery prior/i` AND a table with `Episode | Drawdown | … | Recovery | …` headers.\n- **Render:** Inline SVG scatter on (recovery duration in months × drawdown %). One dot per episode, coloured by severity band (`≤20% → --warn`, `20–40% → --danger`, `>40% → --danger` saturated). Source table sits below as canonical legend.\n- **Why scatter, not horizontal time-bar:** Source data is magnitude × duration, not calendar bounds. Scatter encodes \"how deep × how long\" directly.\n- **Markdown change:** None. Both §7 tables match.\n\n## Slicing — three implementation slices, lowest-risk first\n\nThe slicing order exercises infrastructure under known-correct conditions before any new visual logic ships, so a regression in one slice doesn't compound into the next.\n\n**Slice 1 — promotions only (P21, P22).** Lift ASML's inline CSS into the catalogue and re-key to shell tokens. No new visual logic; the rendering tree is what ASML.html already produces, just driven from markdown. Dark mode starts working everywhere it didn't before, and GOOG.html immediately gains both sections. Common implementation primitive: a numeric-cell parser (`~35%`, `−10–20%`, `~14 months` → numeric value). Build the parser once, then each pattern is ~30 lines of SVG generation. No detection ambiguity — each pattern has a unique header-column signature.\n\n**Slice 3 — narrative + frontmatter patterns (P19, P23).** P19 has the strictest detection rule in the set (three concurrent conditions) and consumes free-form prose; P23 reads from frontmatter and depends on P9's parser. Both are the highest-risk patterns; saving them for last gets infrastructure confidence first.\n\nEach slice is one PR / one Linear issue. A new Linear issue should be created per slice under the Equity Skill Pack project, scoped to the patterns it lands plus the re-render of GOOG.html and ASML.html for verification.\n\n## What this plan does NOT change\n\n- **Frontmatter schema and override values.** `base_wacc`, `growth_ceiling`, `terminal_margin`, `confidence_anchor`, `scenario_axes` numerics, and narrative strings are all untouched. P23 reads them; it does not write them.\n- **Playbook markdown bodies.** Zero changes to GOOG.md or ASML.md. P17 (risks table) needs a `<table>` with `Risk / Severity / Mitigation` columns — playbook failure modes are bullets, never tables. No collisions.\n- **Other consumers of the pattern catalogue.** Pattern names are prefixed `p-` per the catalogue convention; no class-name collisions with the host shell, the existing patterns, or hand-authored content elsewhere.\n- **External data sources.** No new yfinance / EDGAR / web fetches. All visual data lives in the markdown or the frontmatter the markdown already carries.\n\n## Verification\n\nAfter each slice, the following must pass:\n\n1. **Pattern catalogue parses and is consistent.** Each new entry has the six-part structure (Name, Detect, HTML, CSS, Accessibility, When to use / not). All CSS uses only documented skeleton tokens. No hex literals in pattern CSS. Verify by grepping the appended block for `#[0-9a-f]{3,6}` and confirming zero matches.\n2. **Self-containment preserved.** Re-rendered GOOG.html and ASML.html have zero `<link rel=\"stylesheet\">`, zero `<script src=>`, zero remote `<img>` URLs. Use the existing skill's Step 6 gate.\n3. **Symmetry test.** Re-render both playbooks. Open side-by-side. The patterns landed in the current slice produce visually equivalent treatment in both files. For Slice 1 specifically: GOOG.html now has axis cards and failure-mode cards that visually match ASML.html (modulo content differences).\n4. **Detection precision.** No pattern fires on unrelated H2/table content. Spot-check by running each pattern's detect regex against the other playbook's sections and any other markdown the team has (DESIGN.md, CHARTER.md, docs/roadmap.md) — none should match.\n5. **Dark mode + print.** Open re-rendered files with `prefers-color-scheme: dark` (DevTools rendering panel). All new patterns invert correctly. Print preview shows no black-on-black or white-on-white.\n6. **Accessibility.** Every inline SVG has `role=\"img\"` and a populated `aria-label`. Every chart pattern has a co-located source `<table>` or paragraph that carries the canonical data. Run an axe/lighthouse audit if available.\n7. **Future-ticker test.** Create a 30-line scratch playbook stub with the standard 7-section structure and minimal content (one segment, one catalyst, one axis, one failure mode, one episode). Render it. All seven patterns should activate. This is the gold-standard test that the patterns are reusable, not just GOOG/ASML-specific.\n8. **No regressions in existing patterns.** Re-render an existing non-playbook doc that exercises P1–P17 (e.g. one of the pde-skills design docs). Visual output identical to its previous render.\n\n## Follow-up (out of scope for this plan)\n\n- **Linear issues.** Create three Linear issues under the Equity Skill Pack project (ABA team), one per slice, attached to the current cycle. Title pattern: \"Playbook patterns slice N — P21+P22 / P18+P20+P24 / P19+P23\". Update each to In Progress when the slice starts, Done only after the slice is committed AND pushed.\n- **Playbook authoring conventions.** Once the patterns land, document the markdown conventions that activate them as a short section in `playbooks/README.md` (create if absent) so a future agent authoring a new ticker playbook gets the visual treatment by writing the standard shape.\n- **META playbook upgrade.** META.md currently does not match the canonical structure. After P18–P24 are catalogued, META can be brought up to the same bar with the same zero-markdown-change benefit — but this is a separate plan.\n- **Per-skill annotations.** Once P18–P24 are stable, the `/pde-render-html` skill's \"Workflow Step 4\" could optionally reference a \"playbook profile\" so the skill author knows which patterns target this artefact type. Not load-bearing; a UX nicety.\n- **Pattern P17 trigger relaxation.** P17 currently requires the failure-modes content to be a markdown table. After P22 lands, P17 stays as-is — but if a future playbook author writes a Risk/Severity/Mitigation table inside the §5 section, both could attempt to fire. ### P24 — Reset-and-recover scatter (§7)

- **Detect:** H2 matching `/historical reset|reset[- ]and[- ]recover|recovery prior/i` AND a table with `Episode | Drawdown | … | Recovery | …` headers.
- **Render:** Inline SVG scatter on (recovery duration in months × drawdown %). One dot per episode, coloured by severity band (`≤20% → --warn`, `20–40% → --danger`, `>40% → --danger` saturated). Source table sits below as canonical legend.
- **Why scatter, not horizontal time-bar:** Source data is magnitude × duration, not calendar bounds. Scatter encodes "how deep × how long" directly.
- **Markdown change:** None. Both §7 tables match.

## Slicing — three implementation slices, lowest-risk first

The slicing order exercises infrastructure under known-correct conditions before any new visual logic ships, so a regression in one slice doesn't compound into the next.

**Slice 1 — promotions only (P21, P22).** Lift ASML's inline CSS into the catalogue and re-key to shell tokens. No new visual logic; the rendering tree is what ASML.html already produces, just driven from markdown. Dark mode starts working everywhere it didn't before, and GOOG.html immediately gains both sections. Verification surface: 2 playbooks × 2 sections = 4 cases, each comparable to the existing ASML.html snapshot.

**Slice 2 — table-driven inline charts (P18, P20, P24).** Three patterns that decorate existing markdown tables with inline SVG. Common implementation primitive: a numeric-cell parser (`~35%`, `−10–20%`, `~14 months` → numeric value). Build the parser once, then each pattern is ~30 lines of SVG generation. No detection ambiguity — each pattern has a unique header-column signature.

**Slice 3 — narrative + frontmatter patterns (P19, P23).** P19 has the strictest detection rule in the set (three concurrent conditions) and consumes free-form prose; P23 reads from frontmatter and depends on P9's parser. Both are the highest-risk patterns; saving them for last gets infrastructure confidence first.

Each slice is one PR / one Linear issue. A new Linear issue should be created per slice under the Equity Skill Pack project, scoped to the patterns it lands plus the re-render of GOOG.html and ASML.html for verification.

## What this plan does NOT change

- **Frontmatter schema and override values.** `base_wacc`, `growth_ceiling`, `terminal_margin`, `confidence_anchor`, `scenario_axes` numerics, and narrative strings are all untouched. P23 reads them; it does not write them.
- **Playbook markdown bodies.** Zero changes to GOOG.md or ASML.md. All seven detection rules trigger on the current content.
- **The `/pde-render-html` skill workflow.** Steps 1–7 stay the same. P18–P24 are read as part of Step 4's pattern-table lookup, just like P1–P17 already are.
- **Existing patterns P1–P17.** No edits to existing pattern entries. P18–P24 sit at the end of the catalogue and inherit the existing first-match-wins ordering. Conflicts checked: P4 (NFR table) needs `Target / SLO / p95 / Latency` headers — none appear in playbook tables. P17 (risks table) needs a `<table>` with `Risk / Severity / Mitigation` columns — playbook failure modes are bullets, never tables. No collisions.
- **Other consumers of the pattern catalogue.** Pattern names are prefixed `p-` per the catalogue convention; no class-name collisions with the host shell, the existing patterns, or hand-authored content elsewhere.
- **External data sources.** No new yfinance / EDGAR / web fetches. All visual data lives in the markdown or the frontmatter the markdown already carries.

## Verification

After each slice, the following must pass:

1. **Pattern catalogue parses and is consistent.** Each new entry has the six-part structure (Name, Detect, HTML, CSS, Accessibility, When to use / not). All CSS uses only documented skeleton tokens. No hex literals in pattern CSS. Verify by grepping the appended block for `#[0-9a-f]{3,6}` and confirming zero matches.
2. **Self-containment preserved.** Re-rendered GOOG.html and ASML.html have zero `<link rel="stylesheet">`, zero `<script src=>`, zero remote `<img>` URLs. Use the existing skill's Step 6 gate.
3. **Symmetry test.** Re-render both playbooks. Open side-by-side. The patterns landed in the current slice produce visually equivalent treatment in both files. For Slice 1 specifically: GOOG.html now has axis cards and failure-mode cards that visually match ASML.html (modulo content differences).
4. **Detection precision.** No pattern fires on unrelated H2/table content. Spot-check by running each pattern's detect regex against the other playbook's sections and any other markdown the team has (DESIGN.md, CHARTER.md, docs/roadmap.md) — none should match.
5. **Dark mode + print.** Open re-rendered files with `prefers-color-scheme: dark` (DevTools rendering panel). All new patterns invert correctly. Print preview shows no black-on-black or white-on-white.
6. **Accessibility.** Every inline SVG has `role="img"` and a populated `aria-label`. Every chart pattern has a co-located source `<table>` or paragraph that carries the canonical data. Run an axe/lighthouse audit if available.
7. **Future-ticker test.** Create a 30-line scratch playbook stub with the standard 7-section structure and minimal content (one segment, one catalyst, one axis, one failure mode, one episode). Render it. All seven patterns should activate. This is the gold-standard test that the patterns are reusable, not just GOOG/ASML-specific.
8. **No regressions in existing patterns.** Re-render an existing non-playbook doc that exercises P1–P17 (e.g. one of the pde-skills design docs). Visual output identical to its previous render.

## Follow-up (out of scope for this plan)

- **Linear issues.** Create three Linear issues under the Equity Skill Pack project (ABA team), one per slice, attached to the current cycle. Title pattern: "Playbook patterns slice N — P21+P22 / P18+P20+P24 / P19+P23". Update each to In Progress when the slice starts, Done only after the slice is committed AND pushed.
- **Playbook authoring conventions.** Once the patterns land, document the markdown conventions that activate them as a short section in `playbooks/README.md` (create if absent) so a future agent authoring a new ticker playbook gets the visual treatment by writing the standard shape.
- **META playbook upgrade.** META.md currently does not match the canonical structure. After P18–P24 are catalogued, META can be brought up to the same bar with the same zero-markdown-change benefit — but this is a separate plan.
- **Per-skill annotations.** Once P18–P24 are stable, the `/pde-render-html` skill's "Workflow Step 4" could optionally reference a "playbook profile" so the skill author knows which patterns target this artefact type. Not load-bearing; a UX nicety.
- **Pattern P17 trigger relaxation.** P17 currently requires the failure-modes content to be a markdown table. After P22 lands, P17 stays as-is — but if a future playbook author writes a Risk/Severity/Mitigation table inside the §5 section, both could attempt to fire. Pattern ordering (P17 before P22) gives P17 priority, which is the right behaviour. Worth documenting explicitly in the P22 catalogue entry.

15	# HTML pattern catalogue
16	
17	The render-html skill walks the markdown body section by section. For each section, it checks the patterns below in order. The **first match wins** — if no pattern matches, the section renders with the shell's prose defaults (which are themselves styled — see `html-skeleton.md`).
18	
19	Every pattern is defined by:
20	
21	1. **Detect** — the markdown signal that triggers the treatment. Cheap to check; conservative (false-negative is fine, false-positive is bad — wrongly-treated content is harder to debug than untreated).
22	2. **HTML** — the output markup. All class names are prefixed `p-` so they don't collide with the shell's utilities.
23	3. **CSS** — additions appended to the shell's inline `<style>` block. The shell's prose styles remain the fallback; pattern CSS only adds, never overrides.
24	
25	The hard self-containment rule from `html-skeleton.md` applies to every pattern: no external CSS, no external JS, no remote images. Inline SVG is preferred for visual elements. Colour tokens come from the shell's `:root` palette (`--accent`, `--ok`, `--warn`, `--info`, `--danger`, each with a `-soft` variant) — patterns must not introduce ad-hoc hex values.

29	## P1 — Alternatives considered → side-by-side cards
30	
31	**Detect.** A section whose heading text matches `/alternatives?( considered)?/i`, OR a section containing two-to-four sibling H3s each followed by a bulleted list whose first item starts with `Pros:` or `Cons:` (case-insensitive). Maximum four columns — beyond that, fall back to prose (columns become unreadable). **Does not match** ADR `Rationale` sections whose options use bold-paragraph headers (`**Why X:**`) rather than H3 — those go to P11.
32	
33	**HTML.** Each alternative becomes a hover-state card in an auto-fit grid; pros/cons/cost/reversibility render as a small definition list inside.
34	
35	```html
36	<div class="p-alt-grid">
37	  <article class="p-alt-card">
38	    <header><h3>Alternative A — short name</h3><span class="p-alt-verdict p-alt-verdict-chosen">Chosen</span></header>
39	    <dl>
40	      <dt>Pros</dt><dd><ul><li>…</li></ul></dd>
41	      <dt>Cons</dt><dd><ul><li>…</li></ul></dd>
42	      <dt>Cost</dt><dd>…</dd>
43	      <dt>Reversibility</dt><dd>…</dd>
44	    </dl>
45	  </article>
46	  <!-- repeat per alternative -->
47	</div>
48	```
49	
50	The verdict pill (`Chosen` / `Rejected` / em-dash) is optional — apply only if the source explicitly marks one option as chosen.
51	
52	**CSS.**
53	
54	```css
55	.p-alt-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr)); gap: 16px; margin: 20px 0; }
56	.p-alt-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 10px; padding: 18px 20px; transition: border-color 0.15s, transform 0.15s; }
57	.p-alt-card:hover { border-color: var(--accent); }
58	.p-alt-card > header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
59	.p-alt-card h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
60	.p-alt-card dl { margin: 0; }
61	.p-alt-card dt { font-size: 12px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--muted); margin-top: 12px; font-weight: 700; }
62	.p-alt-card dd { margin: 4px 0 0; font-size: 15px; color: var(--fg-soft); line-height: 1.55; }
63	.p-alt-card ul { margin: 4px 0; padding-left: 20px; }
64	.p-alt-verdict { font: 700 12px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 4px; }

219	---
220	
221	## P4 — NFRs table → highlighted numeric table
222	
223	**Detect.** Markdown table inside a section whose heading matches `/non-functional|NFRs?/i`, OR any table whose header row contains one of: `Target`, `SLO`, `p95`, `p99`, `Latency`, `Throughput`, `Availability`, `Budget`.
224	
225	**HTML.** Standard `<table>` with `class="p-nfr"`; cells that parse as numbers (optionally with units `ms`, `s`, `%`, `/s`, `KB`, `MB`) get `class="p-num"`.
226	
227	```html
228	<table class="p-nfr">
229	  <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Target</th><th>Current</th></tr></thead>
230	  <tbody>
231	    <tr><td>p95 latency</td><td class="p-num">200 ms</td><td class="p-num">340 ms</td></tr>
232	  </tbody>
233	</table>
234	```
235	
236	**CSS.**
237	
238	```css
239	.p-nfr td.p-num { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; text-align: right; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 14px; }
240	.p-nfr tbody tr:hover { background: var(--rule-soft); }
241	```
242	
243	The shell already styles `<table>` cleanly; P4 only adds numeric-cell alignment + hover. **Accessibility.** Standard table semantics; `<thead>`/`<tbody>` preserved.
244	
245	---
246	
247	## P5 — Open questions → left-accent decision cards
248	
249	**Detect.** Section heading matches `/open questions?|outstanding questions?|to decide|decisions? to make/i`. Body is either a bullet list (one item per question) or a sequence of bold-paragraph headers (`**Do we allow editing?**`) each followed by a short paragraph of context. Optional trailing metadata `(decide with: design, before slice 2)` or `(owner: @anton, due: 2026-06-01)` lifts into a footer line.
250	
251	**HTML.** Each question becomes a vertically-stacked card with a clay accent on the left, a bold question, a context paragraph, and an optional owner/deadline footer in mono.
252	
253	```html
254	<div class="p-questions">
255	  <div class="p-q">
256	    <div class="p-q-title">Do we allow editing, or only delete-and-repost?</div>
257	    <div class="p-q-body">Editing needs an <code>edited_at</code> column and an "edited" affordance. Delete-and-repost is simpler but loses the reply anchor. Leaning toward delete-only for v1.</div>
258	    <div class="p-q-owner">Decide with · design, before slice 2</div>
259	  </div>
260	  <div class="p-q">
261	    <div class="p-q-title">Email digest cadence when a user has the app closed</div>
262	    <div class="p-q-body">Immediate-per-mention will be noisy. Proposal: batch on a 15-minute window, collapse to one email per task, and respect quiet hours from the existing settings table.</div>
263	    <div class="p-q-owner">Decide with · platform, before slice 4</div>
264	  </div>
265	</div>
266	```
267	
268	The `p-q-owner` footer is optional. When metadata isn't present in the source, omit the `<div>` entirely rather than render an empty footer.
269	
270	**CSS.**
271	
272	```css
273	.p-questions { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; margin: 20px 0; max-width: 820px; }
274	.p-q { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-left: 4px solid var(--accent); border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px 20px; }
275	.p-q-title { font-weight: 600; font-size: 15.5px; color: var(--fg); margin-bottom: 6px; }
276	.p-q-body { font-size: 14px; color: var(--fg-soft); line-height: 1.55; }
277	.p-q-body code { font-size: 0.92em; padding: 1px 5px; background: var(--rule-soft); border-radius: 3px; }
278	.p-q-owner { font: 11.5px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; color: var(--muted); margin-top: 10px; }
279	```
280	
281	**Accessibility.** Plain text hierarchy (title → body → owner). The accent border is decorative — the bold title carries the visual weight and reads cleanly on screen readers.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## P6 — Diff / before-after → two-column annotated diff
286	
287	**Detect.** Two adjacent fenced code blocks within the same H3 / paragraph where the first is labelled (in info string or preceding line) `before`, `was`, `old`, `current`, and the second `after`, `now`, `new`, `proposed`. Also: any code block with info string `diff` renders inline with `+`/`-` line colouring.
288	
289	**HTML (two-column).**
290	
291	```html
292	<div class="p-diff">
293	  <div class="p-diff-side p-diff-before">
294	    <header>Before</header>
295	    <pre><code>…</code></pre>
296	  </div>
297	  <div class="p-diff-side p-diff-after">
298	    <header>After</header>
299	    <pre><code>…</code></pre>
300	  </div>
301	</div>
302	```
303	
304	**HTML (inline diff).** Standard `<pre><code class="language-diff">` with each line wrapped: `<span class="p-diff-add">+ …</span>`, `<span class="p-diff-del">- …</span>`.
305	
306	**CSS.**
307	
308	```css
309	.p-diff { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 14px; margin: 20px 0; }
310	.p-diff-side header { font: 700 12px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 8px; }
311	.p-diff-before pre { border-left: 3px solid var(--danger); }
312	.p-diff-after  pre { border-left: 3px solid var(--ok); }
313	.p-diff-add { background: var(--ok-soft); color: var(--ok); display: block; }
314	.p-diff-del { background: var(--danger-soft); color: var(--danger); display: block; }
315	@media (max-width: 720px) { .p-diff { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
316	```
317	
318	**Accessibility.** Headers (`Before` / `After`) carry the meaning; colour stripe is supplemental.
319	
320	---
321	
322	<!-- P7 (Now/Next/Later kanban) and P8 (ICE scores) are out of scope for v1
323	     — they belong to a future render-roadmap skill. P-numbers are not reused;
324	     downstream patterns keep P9–P12 so cross-references stay stable. -->
325	
326	---
327	
328	## P9 — YAML frontmatter → metadata grid (lifted into doc head)
329	
330	**Detect.** Source markdown begins with a YAML frontmatter block delimited by `---` on its own line, before the H1. Common in ADRs and design docs (fields like `id`, `status`, `date`, `authors`, `linear`, `supersedes`).
331	
332	**HTML.** Frontmatter fields **lift into the shell's `{{meta-grid}}` slot** under the doc head — they do not render as a separate block in the body. The shell's `.meta-grid` styles already cover the visual treatment; P9 only specifies the *lifting* behaviour. The `status` field also lifts into `{{header-pills}}` via the P10 pill treatment.
333	
334	```html
335	<!-- inside the shell's <dl class="meta-grid"> -->
336	<dt>id</dt>      <dd>ADR-engagement-modifier-constants</dd>
337	<dt>authors</dt> <dd>Anton Babushkin</dd>
338	<dt>linear</dt>  <dd><a href="https://linear.app/…">ABA-110</a></dd>
339	<dt>supersedes</dt><dd>—</dd>
340	<dt>source</dt>  <dd>docs/adrs/engagement-modifier-constants.md</dd>
341	<dt>rendered</dt><dd>2026-05-17</dd>
342	```
343	
344	`source` and `rendered` are always included; frontmatter fields fold in alphabetically after them, except `status` (which becomes a header pill, not a grid row) and `date` (which becomes a date pill in the header). **Do not drop frontmatter on the floor** — readers use it to anchor the doc.
345	
346	**Accessibility.** Definition-list semantics; screen readers announce each key-value pair.
347	
348	---
349	
350	## P10 — Status / state values → coloured pill
351	
352	**Detect.** A frontmatter `status:` field, OR a top-of-doc bold line matching `/\*\*Status:\*\*\s+(\w+)/i`, OR a single-cell `Status` column in a table. Recognised values (case-insensitive): `accepted`, `proposed`, `draft`, `rejected`, `superseded`, `deprecated`, `flagged`, `ok`.
353	
354	**HTML.** When detected from frontmatter or top-of-doc bold line, the pill **lifts into the shell's `{{header-pills}}` slot** (using the shell's `.pill` utility — no new CSS needed):
355	
356	```html
357	<span class="pill pill-accepted"><span class="dot"></span>Accepted</span>
358	```
359	
360	When detected inside a table cell, render in-place:
361	
362	```html
363	<td><span class="pill pill-accepted"><span class="dot"></span>Accepted</span></td>
364	```
365	
366	The shell already defines `.pill-accepted`, `.pill-proposed`, `.pill-rejected`, `.pill-superseded`, etc. P10 adds no new CSS — it specifies the *detection + placement* contract. **Accessibility.** Label text carries the meaning; colour is supplemental.
367	
368	---
369	
370	## P11 — Rationale "Why X" blocks → hover-state cards
371	
372	**Detect.** A section heading matches `/rationale/i` AND its body contains two-or-more bold-paragraph headers (`**Why X:**` / `**Why not Y:**`) each followed by a bullet list. Common in ADRs that consider multiple alternatives without dedicated H3s per option.
373	
374	**HTML.** Each bold paragraph becomes a card heading; the following list is the card body. Cards stack in a single-column grid (one per row) so each option gets full line-length for its bullets, but pick up an indigo border on hover and a directional chevron in the title — `✓` for `Why X`, `✗` for `Why not Y`.
375	
376	```html
377	<div class="p-why-grid">
378	  <div class="p-why-card p-why-pro">
379	    <h3><span class="p-why-chev">✓</span>Why Rails</h3>
380	    <ul><li>…</li></ul>
381	  </div>
382	  <div class="p-why-card p-why-con">
383	    <h3><span class="p-why-chev">✗</span>Why not a separate frontend</h3>
384	    <ul><li>…</li></ul>
385	  </div>
386	</div>
387	```
388	
389	**CSS.**
390	
391	```css
392	.p-why-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 14px; margin: 20px 0; }
393	.p-why-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 10px; padding: 18px 22px; transition: border-color 0.15s; }
394	.p-why-card:hover { border-color: var(--accent); }
395	.p-why-card h3 { margin: 0 0 14px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; color: var(--fg); }
396	.p-why-chev { font-size: 18px; line-height: 1; font-weight: 700; }
397	.p-why-pro .p-why-chev { color: var(--ok); }
398	.p-why-con .p-why-chev { color: var(--warn); }
399	.p-why-card ul { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
400	.p-why-card li { position: relative; padding: 6px 0 6px 20px; font-size: 15px; color: var(--fg-soft); line-height: 1.6; }
401	.p-why-card li::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 4px; top: 15px; width: 5px; height: 5px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted); }
402	```
403	
404	**Precedence.** P11 ranks below P1 (Alternatives). When both could match (`Rationale` section whose options also have `Pros:`/`Cons:`), P1's side-by-side card grid is the stronger treatment.
405	
406	**Accessibility.** `<h3>` keeps headings in the document outline; lists keep list semantics; chevron is a real text node (not pseudo-content) so screen readers announce it.
407	
408	---
409	
410	## P12 — Labelled rubric cards (C1, C2, FR3 …) → repeated sub-field cards
411	
412	**Detect.** Two or more sibling H3s whose text matches `/^([A-Z]+\d+)\s+[—–-]\s+/` (e.g. `C1 — Deadband: ±2%`, `FR3 — Idempotent writes`, `OQ5 — …`), AND each section repeats the same set of bold-paragraph sub-fields (e.g. **Reasoning**, **Alternative considered**, **Revision trigger**). The identifier prefix (`C`, `FR`, `OQ`, `NFR`, `ADR`) is rendered as a pill on the card header.
413	
414	**HTML.**
415	
416	```html
417	<div class="p-rubric" id="c1">
418	  <h3><span class="p-rubric-id">C1</span> Deadband: ±2% YoY</h3>
419	  <div class="p-rubric-formula">If <code>abs(yoy_change) &lt; 0.02</code>, set <code>direction = 0</code> …</div>
420	  <h4>Reasoning</h4><p>…</p>
421	  <h4>Alternative considered</h4><p>…</p>
422	  <h4>Revision trigger</h4><p>…</p>
423	</div>
424	```
425	
426	The first paragraph (often a one-line formal definition or formula) becomes `p-rubric-formula`. Subsequent bold-paragraph sub-fields become `<h4>` headings inside the card.
427	
428	**CSS.**
429	
430	```css
431	.p-rubric { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-left: 4px solid var(--accent); border-radius: 10px; padding: 18px 22px; margin: 20px 0; transition: border-color 0.15s; }
432	.p-rubric:hover { border-color: var(--accent); }
433	.p-rubric h3 { margin: 0 0 10px; display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: baseline; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
434	.p-rubric-id { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; font-size: 13px; padding: 4px 9px; background: var(--accent); color: white; border-radius: 4px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-weight: 700; }
435	.p-rubric h4 { font: 700 12px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); margin: 16px 0 6px; }
436	.p-rubric-formula { background: var(--accent-soft); border-left: 3px solid var(--accent); padding: 12px 16px; margin: 12px 0; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.55; border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; color: var(--fg); }
437	.p-rubric p { margin: 0 0 10px; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--fg-soft); }
438	```
439	
440	**Why a dedicated pattern.** Plain-prose rendering of a 6-card ADR section (C1–C6 with Reasoning / Alternative / Revision trigger each) produces a wall of repeating H3+H4 that the reader has to mentally segment. The card boundary plus the identifier pill makes "which constant am I reading" answerable at a glance.
441	
442	**Accessibility.** Heading levels (`<h3>` outer, `<h4>` inner) preserve the document outline; the card boundary is decorative.
443	
444	---
445	
446	## P13 — Summary strip → top-of-doc KPI cells
447	
448	**Detect.** The first content block after the doc header is a short bullet list or definition list of 3–6 key:value pairs where keys are short labels (`Effort`, `Surfaces touched`, `New tables`, `Feature flag`, `Owner`, `Decision deadline`, `Cost`, `Status`) and values are short atomic phrases (a duration, a count, a flag name, a date, a dollar figure). Also matches when the source uses a YAML-frontmatter-style block under a `## Summary` or `## At a glance` heading. **Does not apply** when the same shape appears mid-doc — only the first such block lifts into the summary strip; subsequent ones render as ordinary `<dl>`s.
449	
450	**HTML.** Lifts into a 4-up grid directly under the doc head (above the first `<section>`):
451	
452	```html
453	<div class="p-summary">
454	  <div class="p-summary-cell"><div class="p-summary-k">Effort</div><div class="p-summary-v p-summary-v-accent">~2 weeks</div></div>
455	  <div class="p-summary-cell"><div class="p-summary-k">Surfaces touched</div><div class="p-summary-v">3 packages</div></div>
456	  <div class="p-summary-cell"><div class="p-summary-k">New tables</div><div class="p-summary-v">2</div></div>
457	  <div class="p-summary-cell"><div class="p-summary-k">Feature flag</div><div class="p-summary-v">task_comments_v1</div></div>
458	</div>
459	```
460	
461	The first cell's value gets `p-summary-v-accent` when it carries the headline number (effort, cost, deadline) — at most one per strip. Strip auto-collapses to 2-up at narrow widths.
462	
463	**CSS.**
464	
465	```css
466	.p-summary { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); gap: 14px; margin: 0 0 32px; }
467	.p-summary-cell { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px 18px; }
468	.p-summary-k { font: 700 11px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 8px; }
469	.p-summary-v { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg); line-height: 1.3; }
470	.p-summary-v-accent { color: var(--accent); }
471	@media (max-width: 720px) { .p-summary { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } }
472	```
473	
474	**Accessibility.** Each cell is plain text; label and value are independent text nodes. **Why a dedicated pattern.** A plan or design doc that opens with "this will take two weeks, touch three packages, and ship behind `task_comments_v1`" gives every subsequent reader an anchor for "is this proportionate?" before they hit the first detail.
475	
476	---
477	
478	## P14 — Data flow / architecture → inline SVG diagram
479	
480	**Detect.** A section heading matches `/data flow|architecture|sequence|system( context)?|fan[- ]?out|pipeline/i` AND its body contains EITHER (a) a fenced code block tagged ` ```svg ` containing literal `<svg>` markup, OR (b) a markdown description of nodes-and-edges that the agent has already converted to SVG during conversion. The skill **does not** auto-generate SVG from prose — agents author the SVG explicitly when they identify a diagram-worthy concept.
481	
482	**HTML.** The SVG is wrapped in a framed panel with a caption beneath. Solid lines and dashed lines carry semantic meaning by convention; the caption explains the convention used.
483	
484	```html
485	<div class="p-diagram">
486	  <svg viewBox="0 0 860 340" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Comment write path and realtime fan-out">
487	    <defs>
488	      <marker id="arr" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse">
489	        <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10z" fill="currentColor"/>
490	      </marker>
491	      <marker id="arr-accent" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse">
492	        <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10z" fill="var(--accent)"/>
493	      </marker>
494	    </defs>
495	    <!-- Node template -->
496	    <g class="p-node">
497	      <rect x="20" y="20" width="180" height="54" rx="10"/>
498	      <text x="110" y="43" text-anchor="middle" class="p-node-title">&lt;Composer&gt;</text>
499	      <text x="110" y="60" text-anchor="middle" class="p-node-sub">apps/web</text>
500	    </g>
501	    <!-- Edges: stroke="currentColor" = solid request path; class="p-edge-async" = dashed realtime path -->
502	    <path d="M110 74 L110 150" marker-end="url(#arr)" class="p-edge"/>
503	    <path d="M520 177 L660 177" marker-end="url(#arr-accent)" class="p-edge-async"/>
504	    <!-- Edge label -->
505	    <text x="240" y="170" class="p-edge-label">mutate</text>
506	  </svg>
507	  <p class="p-diagram-caption">Solid = request/response. Dashed = realtime fan-out. The composer never waits on the dashed path.</p>
508	</div>
509	```
510	
511	**CSS.**
512	
513	```css
514	.p-diagram { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; margin: 20px 0; overflow-x: auto; }
515	.p-diagram svg { display: block; min-width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; color: var(--muted); }
516	.p-diagram .p-node rect { fill: var(--bg); stroke: var(--rule); stroke-width: 1.5; }
517	.p-diagram .p-node-title { font: 600 12px ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; fill: var(--fg); }
518	.p-diagram .p-node-sub { font: 10.5px ui-monospace, monospace; fill: var(--muted); }
519	.p-diagram .p-edge { stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; }
520	.p-diagram .p-edge-async { stroke: var(--accent); stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 5 4; }
521	.p-diagram .p-edge-label { font: 10.5px ui-monospace, monospace; fill: var(--muted); }
522	.p-diagram-caption { font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--muted); margin: 12px 0 0; line-height: 1.55; }
523	```
524	
525	**Authoring guidance for the agent.** Use the four node-classes (`p-node` for default, `p-node p-node-emphasis` for the persistence layer or any single "focus" box — fills with `var(--fg)` background and `var(--bg)` text). Limit to ~7 nodes and ~10 edges; if the diagram needs more, split it. Edge labels must be ≤ 24 chars; longer explanations go in the caption.
526	
527	**Accessibility.** `<svg role="img" aria-label="…">` provides a short description; the caption beneath provides the long description. Text inside the SVG is selectable. **No remote fonts** — the SVG inherits the page font stack.
528	
529	---
530	
531	## P15 — Mockup frame → labelled UI sketch
532	
533	**Detect.** Section heading matches `/mockup|wireframe|sketch|prototype/i` AND body contains 1–3 sub-blocks separated by H3s or bold paragraph headers that look like artefact labels (`A · Thread inside a task card`, `Variant 1`, `Empty state`). Mockup contents can be either (a) inline HTML the agent has authored to approximate the UI, or (b) an inline SVG sketch.
534	
535	**HTML.** Each mockup is a framed card with a small label bar and a body area. Two-up grid by default; collapses to single column at narrow widths.
536	
537	```html
538	<div class="p-mocks">
539	  <figure class="p-mock">
540	    <figcaption class="p-mock-label">A · Thread inside a task card</figcaption>
541	    <div class="p-mock-body">
542	      <!-- agent-authored UI sketch goes here -->
543	    </div>
544	  </figure>
545	  <figure class="p-mock">
546	    <figcaption class="p-mock-label">B · Sidebar unread digest</figcaption>
547	    <div class="p-mock-body"> … </div>
548	  </figure>
549	</div>
550	```
551	
552	**CSS.**
553	
554	```css
555	.p-mocks { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr)); gap: 20px; margin: 20px 0; }
556	.p-mock { margin: 0; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; }
557	.p-mock-label { padding: 10px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--rule-soft); font: 700 12px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
558	.p-mock-body { padding: 20px; background: var(--bg); }
559	```
560	
561	**Authoring guidance.** Mockups are deliberately sketchy — they exist to align reviewers on layout, not to look pixel-final. Real UI primitives the agent can lean on: rounded `<div>`s for cards, small circular `<div>`s for avatars (initials inside), dashed-border divs for "image goes here," `<input disabled>` for form fields. The aim is "we agree on the shape," not "this is the final design."
562	
563	**Accessibility.** `<figure>` + `<figcaption>` keeps the label tied to the mockup for screen readers. Mockup bodies should be ARIA-`role="presentation"` if they contain non-functional interactive-looking elements (a `<button>` that doesn't do anything is worse than a styled `<div>`).
564	
565	---
566	
567	## P16 — Code panel → file-labelled dark block
568	
569	**Detect.** Any fenced code block that has BOTH (a) an info string naming the language AND (b) a preceding line or paragraph that names a file path (`apps/web/hooks/useAddComment.ts`, `packages/db/migrations/0042_comments.sql`). The file path is detected as a relative-path-looking token containing at least one `/` and ending in a recognised extension. Plain fenced blocks without a file label fall through to the shell's default `<pre>` styling. The P6 two-column diff treatment takes precedence when both apply.
570	
571	**HTML.**
572	
573	```html
574	<figure class="p-code">
575	  <figcaption class="p-code-file">apps/web/hooks/useAddComment.ts</figcaption>
576	  <pre class="p-code-body"><code class="language-ts">…</code></pre>
577	</figure>
578	```
579	
580	When two or more code panels appear in the same section back-to-back, they render in a 2-up grid so reviewers can scan them in parallel (e.g. migration + hook):
581	
582	```html
583	<div class="p-code-grid">
584	  <figure class="p-code"> … </figure>
585	  <figure class="p-code"> … </figure>
586	</div>
587	```
588	
589	**CSS.**
590	
591	```css
592	.p-code { margin: 16px 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
593	.p-code-file { font: 12px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; color: var(--muted); margin-bottom: 8px; }
594	.p-code-body { background: var(--fg); color: #e8e6de; border-radius: 12px; padding: 18px 20px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0; }
595	.p-code-body code { font: 12.5px/1.65 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; color: inherit; background: transparent; padding: 0; }
596	.p-code-body .tok-kw  { color: var(--accent); }
597	.p-code-body .tok-str { color: var(--ok); }
598	.p-code-body .tok-cm  { color: var(--muted); font-style: italic; }
599	.p-code-body .tok-fn  { color: #c9b98a; }
600	.p-code-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 20px; margin: 16px 0; }
601	@media (max-width: 900px) { .p-code-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
602	```
603	
604	**Token wrapping.** The agent applies four span classes inline (`tok-kw` for keywords, `tok-str` for string literals, `tok-cm` for comments, `tok-fn` for function/identifier names). Don't attempt full lexer-grade highlighting — the four tokens are enough to give the panel hierarchy without misleading the reader. If the agent isn't confident about a token, leave it un-spanned (the default body colour reads cleanly).
605	
606	**Accessibility.** `<figure>` + `<figcaption>` ties the file path to the code. Dark background + light text passes AA at 14.5:1 (`#e8e6de` on `var(--fg)` `#0a0a0f`).
607	
608	---
609	
610	## P17 — Risks & mitigations → severity-tagged table
611	
612	**Detect.** Section heading matches `/risks?( ?(and|&) ?mitigations?)?|threats?|failure modes?/i` AND body is a markdown table with at least these columns (case-insensitive, partial match OK): `Risk` (or `Description`), `Severity` (or `Sev` / `Likelihood`), `Mitigation` (or `Response`). An optional `Owner` column is preserved. Severity values are matched against `high|med(ium)?|low|critical` (case-insensitive).
613	
614	**HTML.** Three- or four-column grid (not a real `<table>`, because we want the severity cell to be a chip in a narrow centred column). Borders form the visual table.
615	
616	```html
617	<div class="p-risks">
618	  <div class="p-risks-row p-risks-head">
619	    <div>Risk</div><div>Sev</div><div>Mitigation</div>
620	  </div>
621	  <div class="p-risks-row">
622	    <div>Realtime duplicate: socket append races with HTTP response.</div>
623	    <div><span class="p-sev p-sev-high">HIGH</span></div>
624	    <div>Dedupe on server-assigned <code>id</code>; temp rows filtered on reconcile.</div>
625	  </div>
626	  <!-- repeat rows -->
627	</div>
628	```
629	
630	**CSS.**
631	
632	```css
633	.p-risks { border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--surface); margin: 20px 0; }
634	.p-risks-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.6fr 80px 1.6fr; }
635	.p-risks-row + .p-risks-row { border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
636	.p-risks-row > div { padding: 14px 18px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--fg-soft); }
637	.p-risks-row > div + div { border-left: 1px solid var(--rule); }
638	.p-risks-head > div { background: var(--rule-soft); color: var(--fg); font: 700 12px/1 "Inter", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 12px 18px; }
639	.p-sev { display: inline-block; font: 700 11px/1 ui-monospace, monospace; padding: 4px 9px; border-radius: 6px; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
640	.p-sev-high     { background: var(--danger-soft); color: var(--danger); }
641	.p-sev-critical { background: var(--danger);      color: white; }
642	.p-sev-med      { background: var(--warn-soft);   color: var(--warn); }
643	.p-sev-low      { background: var(--ok-soft);     color: var(--ok); }
644	@media (max-width: 720px) {
645	  .p-risks-row { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
646	  .p-risks-row > div + div { border-left: none; border-top: 1px dashed var(--rule); }
647	  .p-risks-head { display: none; }
648	}
649	```
650	
651	**Optional owner column.** When the source table has an Owner column, switch the grid to `1.5fr 80px 1.5fr 120px` and add a fourth `<div>` per row. Owner renders as plain text or a `pill pill-meta` if it looks like a handle (`@anton`).
652	
653	**Accessibility.** Severity label text (`HIGH` / `MED` / `LOW`) carries the meaning; colour is supplemental. The grid uses `<div>`s rather than `<table>` because the severity column is intentionally narrow and centre-aligned — a real table here forces awkward column-width compromises. Screen readers still announce each row's content in order; for users who require table semantics, the source markdown table is the canonical form.
654	
655	---
656	
657	## Fallback
658	
659	A section that matches no pattern renders with the shell's section-header treatment (`<section class="s"><header><span class="ix">NN</span><h2>…</h2></header>`) and the shell's prose defaults (`<p>`, `<ul>`, `<table>`, `<pre>`, `<blockquote>`). The fallback is "well-typeset doc," not raw HTML — false-positive pattern matches degrade review trust faster than missing treatments.
660	
661	## Adding a new pattern
662	
663	When a new pattern earns its slot:
664	
665	1. Add a section here following the same six-part structure: heading, **Detect**, **HTML**, **CSS**, **Accessibility**, brief rationale.
666	2. Number it sequentially (`P13 — …`) so cross-references stay stable.
667	3. Confirm the CSS uses shell colour tokens (`--accent`, `--ok`, `--warn`, `--info`, `--danger`, `-soft` variants) — no ad-hoc hex values.
668	4. Confirm the CSS only adds new selectors prefixed `p-` — it must not override any rule in `html-skeleton.md`.
669	5. If the detection signal could overlap an existing pattern, document the precedence rule explicitly. The first-match-wins ordering of this file is the resolution mechanism.
670	
```

25	# ASML Playbook
26	
27	**Coverage status:** ESTABLISHED · INFRASTRUCTURE  
28	**Thesis in one line:** EUV monopoly + High-NA ramp + China export-control overhang, with the semiconductor capex cycle as the dominant input.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## 1. Business Architecture
33	
34	### Segment mix (approximate FY2025 basis)
35	
36	| Segment | Revenue share | Growth trajectory |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| EUV systems (standard + High-NA) | ~50% | Cycle-dependent; High-NA ramp adds a step-up from 2026 |
39	| Advanced DUV (immersion) | ~25% | Mature; sensitive to logic node digestion pace |
40	| Mature DUV (dry, KrF, i-line) | ~10% | Stable; exposed to auto / industrial / mature-node capex |
41	| Installed Base Management (IBM) — services + upgrades | ~15% | Most defensive; ~25% of revenue; less cyclical than new tool orders |
42	
43	IBM (Installed Base Management) is the earnings-floor segment: service contracts and upgrades on the ~4,000-tool installed base continue regardless of new-system order cycles. It is the component most vulnerable to a China-service-rule tightening scenario (see Failure Modes).
44	
45	### Key revenue drivers
46	
47	1. **EUV unit shipments** — the volume metric for leading-edge logic. Consensus expects a step-up to ~90–100 units/year by 2027 from ~50–60 in 2024; below-60 for two consecutive years is a bearish inflection signal.
48	2. **High-NA EUV ramp** — ASP (Average Selling Price) per High-NA tool is ~€350M vs ~€200M for standard EUV. Even 5 additional High-NA units/year moves blended ASP materially. First customer is TSMC; Intel and Samsung are expected second/third.
49	3. **China revenue share** — ranged 20–49% of system revenue (2022–2023 peak) before export-control restrictions; tracking ~15–20% under current rules. Further rule tightening is the bear-case revenue risk; stabilisation at current levels is the base case.
50	4. **IBM attach rate** — services revenue as % of cumulative installed base value. Rising attach rate signals customer utilisation and confidence; falling attach rate (e.g., from China service restrictions) is the canary in the earnings-floor thesis.
51	
52	### End-market exposure
53	
54	- **Leading-edge logic (HPC/AI + smartphones):** TSMC, Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry — drive EUV and High-NA demand
55	- **Memory (DRAM + NAND):** SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung Memory — drive EUV-for-DRAM and advanced-patterning demand
56	- **Mature logic / specialty:** auto, industrial, IoT via mature DUV (less cyclically exposed but not immune)
57	
58	Customer concentration: TSMC + Samsung + Intel represent the dominant share of EUV system revenue. [TODO: verify exact top-3/top-5 % against latest ASML 20-F / annual report risk-factor disclosure — do not cite a specific number without verification]
59	
60	---
61	
62	## 2. Capex-Cycle Position
63	
64	ASML is in a **cycle-trough / inflection** phase as of mid-2026. The 2024–2025 digestion period (customers pausing orders after COVID-era over-ordering of DUV tools) is expected to trough in 2026, with re-acceleration in 2027–2029 on two overlapping drivers:
65	
66	1. **AI-driven advanced-node demand:** TSMC N2/N2P, Samsung 2GAP, Intel 18A ramps require sustained EUV intensity. Hyperscaler custom-silicon fabs (Google, Meta, Amazon) are incremental new demand on top of smartphone-driven baseline.
67	2. **High-NA volume ramp:** First High-NA tools are being qualified at TSMC Arizona and Intel Ohio. If High-NA economics validate (cost-per-wafer clears vs multi-patterning DUV), the step-up in ASP per unit creates a revenue tailwind independent of unit-volume growth.
68	
69	**Normalised-margin thesis:** The `terminal_margin` override of 30% assumes High-NA reaches mature unit economics, customer utilisation normalises post-trough, and customer-prepayment working-capital swings dampen over a full cycle. TTM clean FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin (~24%) is trough-distorted by both the demand digestion period and ramp-related investment; anchoring the DCF on TTM understates steady-state. The 30% base sits between TTM clean FCF (~24%) and TTM earnings margin (~35%, implied by P/E 49.5 / P/S 17.18) — a defensible midpoint.
70	
71	**Bear case:** If High-NA economics fail to clear at scale OR if the semi cycle air-pocket is deeper than expected, utilisation stays weak and terminal margin compresses to TTM-clean levels. This is exactly what `scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.24` captures — it anchors the bear terminal margin at the observed trough rather than at a symmetric ±delta from base.
72	
73	**Cycle re-acceleration signal:** The evidence-gating condition for the base-case trough-and-re-acceleration thesis is three concurrent observables: (a) SEMI book-to-bill ratio sustained above 1.2 for ≥2 consecutive quarters; (b) ASML's quarterly earnings commentary guiding EUV unit shipments toward ≥70 units/year run-rate; (c) published guidance confirming the 2030 LRP (Long-Range Plan) envelope without downward revision at a Capital Markets Day event. A ratio that stays below 1.0 and LRP guidance that steps down by FY2028 would constitute evidence for the extended-digestion bear case rather than a V-shaped recovery.
74
