353	<section id="sell-side-axes">
354	  <h2>4. Sell-Side Disagreement Axes</h2>
355	  <p>The real arguments the sell-side is having on ASML right now. Each axis identifies what distinguishes recoverable cycle noise from a thesis-breaking structural signal.</p>
356	
357	  <div class="axis-card">
358	    <div class="axis-head">
359	      <h3 id="axis-1">1. Capex-cycle trough timing</h3>
360	      <p class="axis-q">Does the semiconductor capex cycle trough in H2 2026 and re-accelerate cleanly into 2027&#8211;2028, or is digestion deeper and longer &#8212; extending into 2027&#8211;2028 on memory oversupply and smartphone demand weakness?</p>
361	    </div>
362	    <div class="axis-body">
363	      <div class="axis-views">
364	        <div class="axis-view bull-view">
365	          <div class="view-label">Bull</div>
366	          TSMC has sustained its 2025 and 2026 capex guidance across multiple earnings calls; SK Hynix is proceeding with HBM3E expansions despite DRAM pricing softness; AI-driven advanced-node demand is pulling forward leading-edge EUV tool orders. A V-shaped re-acceleration beginning H1 2027 is consistent with prior semi-cycle trough-to-recovery timelines (2019 trough recovered in ~14 months; 2022&#8211;2023 trough recovered in ~12 months).
367	        </div>
368	        <div class="axis-view bear-view">
369	          <div class="view-label">Bear</div>
370	          Memory oversupply (DRAM/NAND inventory digestion) is slower-than-consensus; smartphone unit demand remains soft and depresses mature-node utilisation; Intel&#8217;s financial difficulties and delayed 18A ramp reduce one of the three leading-edge anchor customers. In this scenario the digestion period extends to 2027&#8211;2028, producing an L-shaped trough rather than a V, and ASML&#8217;s unit volume misses the upper-LRP trajectory by 2+ years.
371	        </div>
372	      </div>
373	      <div class="nvs">
374	        <div class="nvs-label">Noise vs. Structural</div>
375	        A single quarter of order intake recovery or SEMI book-to-bill above 1.0 is noise &#8212; quarterly lumpiness in order timing is normal. Structural re-acceleration signal requires all three simultaneously: (a) SEMI book-to-bill sustained above 1.2 for &#8805;2 consecutive quarters; (b) ASML&#8217;s own published EUV unit shipment guidance pointing to &#8805;70 units/year run-rate; (c) no downward revision to the 2030 LRP envelope in a Capital Markets Day event. Any one criterion alone is insufficient.
376	      </div>
377	    </div>
378	  </div>
379	
380	  <div class="axis-card">
381	    <div class="axis-head">
382	      <h3 id="axis-2">2. High-NA economics at scale</h3>
383	      <p class="axis-q">Will High-NA EUV cost-per-wafer clear the threshold where customers prefer it to multi-patterning DUV at volume production &#8212; or does the crossover point remain too far out to support the post-2027 unit-growth and ASP premise?</p>
384	    </div>
385	    <div class="axis-body">
386	      <div class="axis-views">
387	        <div class="axis-view bull-view">
388	          <div class="view-label">Bull</div>
389	          TSMC&#8217;s public endorsement and Intel&#8217;s production commitments for High-NA are not speculative &#8212; both have qualified High-NA tools for their most advanced nodes. The cost-per-wafer equation improves on learning curves: lithography steps collapse from 4&#8211;6 DUV multi-patterning passes to a single High-NA pass, reducing process complexity, cycle time, and defect probability. Even before full cost crossover, High-NA enables EUV-only nodes that multi-patterning DUV cannot achieve &#8212; making adoption a technical requirement, not a pure economics decision.
390	        </div>
391	        <div class="axis-view bear-view">
392	          <div class="view-label">Bear</div>
393	          High-NA tools are &#8364;350M+ per unit vs ~&#8364;200M for standard EUV &#8212; a 75% ASP premium that must be recovered through wafer-cost savings. Early yield data is not publicly disclosed; learning curves at initial production yields are slower than mature EUV yields, and the cost crossover point is sensitive to yield improvement pace assumptions. Multi-patterning DUV is proven technology; Intel and TSMC retain the option to extend it for one additional node generation if High-NA economics don&#8217;t validate quickly enough.
394	        </div>
395	      </div>
396	      <div class="nvs">
397	        <div class="nvs-label">Noise vs. Structural</div>
398	        ASML&#8217;s quarterly High-NA unit shipment count is the primary observable. Fewer than 5 High-NA units shipped in 2027 indicates adoption materially below the bull-case trajectory, but could still reflect timing delays rather than economic rejection. A structural signal requires a qualitative threshold event: a major customer (TSMC or Intel) publicly reducing its High-NA unit plan, or announcing a reversion to multi-patterning DUV for a node previously committed to High-NA. No such event has occurred as of Q1 2026. The bear case today is a timing risk &#8212; not yet a thesis-breaking failure.
399	      </div>
400	    </div>
401	  </div>
402	
403	  <div class="axis-card">
404	    <div class="axis-head">
405	      <h3 id="axis-3">3. China revenue durability</h3>
406	      <p class="axis-q">Is 15&#8211;20% China revenue a stable floor under the current export-control framework, or will progressive rule-tightening &#8212; particularly an extension to DUV service/spare-parts &#8212; erode it further toward 5&#8211;10%?</p>
407	    </div>
408	    <div class="axis-body">
409	      <div class="axis-views">
410	        <div class="axis-view bull-view">
411	          <div class="view-label">Bull</div>
412	          Current export controls primarily restrict new EUV system sales and the most advanced DUV (immersion) systems. The existing DUV installed base in China continues to generate service, maintenance, and spare-parts revenue under current rules. SMIC and other Chinese fabs are expanding mature-node capacity on the DUV installed base; utilisation of existing tools supports ongoing IBM attach revenue. The bull case requires no relaxation of current rules &#8212; simply that no further expansion occurs.
413	        </div>
414	        <div class="axis-view bear-view">
415	          <div class="view-label">Bear</div>
416	          The export-control framework is ratcheting incrementally: 2023 EUV ban, 2024 advanced-DUV restriction, with the next logical policy step being service/spare-parts supply restriction on the DUV installed base already in China. Each incremental tightening reduces the addressable revenue pool. The bear case is that China revenue converges toward 5&#8211;10% (service on increasingly restriction-impaired installed base) rather than stabilising at 15&#8211;20%, compressing IBM revenue simultaneously with new-system revenue.
417	        </div>
418	      </div>
419	      <div class="nvs">
420	        <div class="nvs-label">Noise vs. Structural</div>
421	        Quarter-to-quarter China revenue fluctuation is noise &#8212; order timing, tool delivery schedules, FX, and pre-cutoff order pull-forward all create lumpiness. Structural erosion signal requires a binary event: a formally announced and implemented rule expansion that explicitly covers service or spare-parts supply to the existing DUV installed base in China. The sell-side range on China&#8217;s 2027 revenue contribution spans roughly 8&#8211;22% &#8212; this width reflects genuine policy uncertainty, not analytical disagreement on existing data.
422	      </div>
423	    </div>
424	  </div>
425	
426	  <div class="axis-card">
427	    <div class="axis-head">
428	      <h3 id="axis-4">4. TAM ceiling &#8212; real or expandable?</h3>
429	      <p class="axis-q">Does ASML&#8217;s 2030 LRP implying ~$28B advanced-logic equipment TAM at ~86% EUV penetration represent a hard ceiling, or is the addressable TAM itself expanding through new lithography demand vectors not captured in the LRP?</p>
430	    </div>
431	    <div class="axis-body">
432	      <div class="axis-views">
433	        <div class="axis-view bull-view">
434	          <div class="view-label">Bull</div>
435	          The TAM is dynamic. Three expansion vectors are visible beyond the LRP baseline: (a) <strong>3D-DRAM and multi-layer NAND</strong> architectures raise EUV-intensity per wafer as vertical complexity increases; (b) <strong>advanced packaging</strong> formats (HBM stacks, glass substrate interposers, chiplet-to-chiplet interconnects) require new lithography steps not present in prior planar-chip LRP planning; (c) <strong>geographic fab proliferation</strong> (TSMC Arizona, Samsung Taylor, Intel Ohio, Rapidus Japan, European IPCEI fabs) creates new-customer tool purchase demand. If additive to the LRP, effective TAM is $32&#8211;36B+ rather than $28B.
436	        </div>
437	        <div class="axis-view bear-view">
438	          <div class="view-label">Bear</div>
439	          ASML&#8217;s LRP is built with visibility into customer capex plans &#8212; the demand from AI-driven leading-edge fabs, memory complexity growth, and geographic expansion is already modelled by ASML&#8217;s internal planning team and reflected in the LRP envelope. If the LRP already captures these demand vectors, the bull thesis for above-LRP revenue requires a specific positive surprise, not just a continuation of stated strategy.
440	        </div>
441	      </div>
442	      <div class="nvs">
443	        <div class="nvs-label">Noise vs. Structural</div>
444	        ASML&#8217;s Capital Markets Day guidance revisions are the primary falsification test. If successive CMD guidance revisions show upward adjustments to memory-EUV tools/year or packaging litho unit count above the prior CMD baseline, that is TAM-expansion confirmation signal. If CMD guidance holds flat or revises down despite visible AI infrastructure investment announcements, it implies the LRP already captured the demand that markets are treating as incremental upside. The forward falsification test is whether the next CMD (expected 2027) revises memory and packaging litho demand above 2025 CMD levels.
445	      </div>
446	    </div>
447	  </div>
448	
449	  <div class="axis-card">
450	    <div class="axis-head">
451	      <h3 id="axis-5">5. IBM (services) growth as the moat anchor</h3>
452	      <p class="axis-q">Is Installed Base Management a durable ~25% revenue floor that grows with the installed base regardless of cycle &#8212; or is the IBM earnings-floor thesis overstated given its exposure to utilisation cycles and China service restrictions?</p>
453	    </div>
454	    <div class="axis-body">
455	      <div class="axis-views">
456	        <div class="axis-view bull-view">
457	          <div class="view-label">Bull</div>
458	          IBM revenue compounds with the installed base: 4,000+ tools in the field, growing at ~100&#8211;150 units/year net, each generating multi-decade service agreements. Customers cannot risk tool downtime at advanced nodes &#8212; ASML service engineers are embedded in fabs, and rapid-response maintenance is mission-critical to fab yield and throughput. This operational embedding creates strong pricing power and high contract renewal rates. IBM has been the most stable revenue segment through prior cycle troughs (2019, 2022&#8211;2023).
459	        </div>
460	        <div class="axis-view bear-view">
461	          <div class="view-label">Bear</div>
462	          IBM has two structural vulnerabilities: First, customer utilisation declines during a broad capex air-pocket reduce upgrade spend &#8212; upgrades are discretionary within the IBM line even if maintenance contracts are not. Second, China service/spare-parts export restrictions would remove the China-installed-base IBM revenue pool discretely rather than gradually &#8212; a non-linear event. The IBM earnings-floor thesis holds only while both customer utilisation is above a minimum threshold and China service rules remain as-is.
463	        </div>
464	      </div>
465	      <div class="nvs">
466	        <div class="nvs-label">Noise vs. Structural</div>
467	        IBM revenue is disclosed quarterly as a named segment line. A single-quarter IBM revenue decline is noise &#8212; seasonal maintenance scheduling, customer-site shutdowns, and FX create quarter-to-quarter lumpiness. Structural IBM impairment signal requires IBM revenue declining year-over-year for &#8805;2 consecutive quarters while ASML&#8217;s total installed base is growing &#8212; this configuration (shrinking IBM on a growing base) indicates attach-rate compression. A China service-restriction announcement is the most decisive binary structural signal: immediately visible in the subsequent quarter&#8217;s China service revenue commentary.
468	      </div>
469	    </div>
470	  </div>
471	</section>

56	
57	### End-market exposure
58	
59	- **Digital advertising (~77% of revenue):** Cyclical sensitivity to global ad-spend budgets; secular tail risk from AI-interface displacement.
60	- **Enterprise cloud (~13% of revenue):** GCP + Workspace; less cyclical; differentiated through Gemini integration.
61	- **Hardware / consumer services (~5%):** Pixel, Google One, Maps API — limited operating leverage.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 2. AI Investment Cycle Position
66	
67	Alphabet spent ~$91B in FY2025 capex, ~70% AI-attributed per public guidance. This depresses TTM clean FCF margin and creates a two-sided uncertainty that is structurally different from a normal capex cycle trough: the normalisation path depends on **which of two competing margin theses proves correct.**
68	
69	**Path A — cost-temporary (base case):**  
70	AI model efficiency improves on hardware and software curves (inference cost-per-query falls as TPUs scale and model compression matures). Capex-as-share-of-revenue mean-reverts post-2027 as the build phase completes. Monetisation density per AI-assisted query holds near current levels or improves (AI Overviews maintain ad slots; AI Mode monetises at comparable RPM (Revenue Per Mille) to standard Search). Terminal margin recovers toward 30% SBC-stripped FCF.
71	
72	**Path B — cost-permanent (bear-case terminal margin thesis):**  
73	AI serving costs do not decay with scale at the rate Path A assumes — either because competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment, or because each AI query is structurally more compute-intensive than a traditional lookup. Simultaneously, AI-style answering reduces click-through rates, compressing ad density and CPC. Revenue growth decelerates while cost stays elevated. Terminal margin stabilises in the low-20s. This is the basis for `scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22`.
74	
75	**Base-case choice:** The playbook picks Path A but does not assume the asymmetry away. The `terminal_margin` base of 30% reflects Path A prevailing. The bear `scenario_axes` captures Path B as a discrete scenario — not a symmetric delta from base — because interface displacement and cost-permanence cause joint compression of both growth and margin simultaneously, which a symmetric ±multiplier cannot represent.
76	
77	**Normalised-margin anchors:** The `terminal_margin` base of 30% sits between two reference points. Reported TTM FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin is severely depressed by the AI build cycle — with ~$91B FY2025 capex, capex-blended group FCF margin is in the low-to-mid single digits (approximate; derived from disclosed capex and operating cash flows). On a normalised-capex, SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped basis — stripping the AI-attributed ~$64B capex increment above estimated pre-AI maintenance capex (~$25B) and SBC (~5–6% of revenue per disclosed annual figures) — clean FCF margin is inferred at approximately 22–27%: this is the distressed-floor reference point under Path A's recovery thesis. Search-segment-implied margin is structurally higher: Search & Other at ~57% of revenue is Alphabet's highest-margin segment, with implied margins above 35% plausible given disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income of ~28–30% (approximate; GAAP segment FCF margins are not separately reported — treat these as order-of-magnitude anchors, not precise figures). The 30% base sits between the normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%) and the Search-segment ceiling (~35%+) — a defensible midpoint under Path A.
78	
79	**AI-capex normalisation signal:** The evidence-gating condition for Path A is a sustained decline in capex/revenue ratio after FY2026, visible across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that re-elevates above FY2025 levels by FY2028 would be evidence for Path B.
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 3. Active Catalysts
84	
85	| Catalyst | Probability | IV impact | Direction |
86	|---|---|---|---|
87	| DOJ Search remedies finalised (default-payment restrictions, Chrome leverage, or divestiture ordered) | ~35% material remedy by end-2027 | −10–20% | Strongly negative — distribution economics impaired |
88	| AI Mode Search query-mix data disclosed showing CPC stability | ~40% by end-2026 | +5–10% | Positive — monetisation-compression bear case weakened |

98	## 4. Sell-Side Disagreement Axes
99	
100	Organised by the **4-layer AI-disruption taxonomy** plus Cloud differentiation. Each axis names what distinguishes temporary noise from structural change.
101	
102	### (i) Interface disruption
103	
104	**The question:** Do AI assistants become the primary discovery and navigation layer, displacing Google Search as the first-place-I-ask interface for high-intent commercial queries?
105	
106	- **Bull:** AI Overviews and AI Mode keep users inside Google surfaces for the queries that generate ad revenue; "where do you start a purchase or research query" surveys remain Google-dominant. Competitors capture curiosity and informational queries, not commercial-intent ones.
107	- **Bear:** AI-native interfaces (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, in-OS assistants, browser-native AI) capture meaningful share of commercial-intent queries — the queries that actually produce CPC revenue. Users who stop clicking to Google for high-intent searches stop generating ad impressions entirely.
108	- **Noise vs. structural:** A single-quarter deceleration in Search revenue growth is noise — ad-cycle effects, macro, seasonality, and mix-shift within Search all produce this. Structural signal requires: monotonic commercial-intent query-share migration **sustained across ≥3 quarters**; "first-place-I-ask" data from third-party consumer panels showing a durable shift (not curiosity queries — specifically purchase-research, product-comparison, local-service-intent); revenue-per-search trend declining even in periods of macro-stable ad spend. All three together constitute structural signal; any one alone is insufficient.
109	
110	### (ii) Monetisation compression
111	
112	**The question:** Even at stable Search query share, does AI-style answering structurally compress revenue-per-search — via fewer ad slots per query, reduced click-through, or lower CPC?
113	
114	- **Bull:** AI Overviews maintain or improve revenue-per-search through better ad-intent matching; users who get AI answers and then click on ads are higher-intent buyers; blended RPM (Revenue Per Mille) holds or expands.

183	## 7. Historical Reset-and-Recover Priors
184	
185	| Episode | Drawdown (approx) | Catalyst | Recovery | Lesson |
186	|---|---|---|---|---|
187	| 2022 ad recession + iOS privacy reset | ~−45% peak-to-trough | Macro ad-spend contraction; Apple ATT (App Tracking Transparency) headwinds to ad-targeting quality | ~12 months; recovery on ad-market rebound and YouTube brand-advertiser return | Cyclical ad recessions recover on macro normalisation; the underlying monetisation mechanics remained intact throughout |
188	| 2023 Bing + ChatGPT integration scare | ~−15% drawdown | Microsoft integrated GPT-4 into Bing; sell-side concern about Search displacement | ~6 months; recovered as Bing share gains remained marginal and Google announced Bard/Gemini roadmap | A credible competitive interface challenge caused a multiple de-rate, but was not sufficient to structurally impair query economics at the monetisation layer |
189	| 2024–2025 DOJ verdict + AI-Mode launch uncertainty | ~−20–25% drawdown (approximate) | DOJ liability finding in Search distribution case; uncertainty around AI Mode cannibalising Search RPM (Revenue Per Mille) | Partial recovery as AI Overviews maintained revenue-per-search in initial disclosed metrics | Regulatory headline risk creates an IV-expansion event; recovery pace correlated with whether monetisation metrics held in the quarters following the ruling |
190	
191	[Note: episode drawdown magnitudes and recovery durations are approximate; verify against price history before citing numerically.]
192	
193	**Mean-reversion implication:** Prior episodes where Google experienced sharp drawdowns and recovered shared a common structural condition: user behaviour at the **Search query layer remained intact**. Ad-cycle recessions compressed revenue per query temporarily; Bing integration scared the multiple but did not move query-source share durably; DOJ rulings de-rated the distribution-moat premium but did not change where users began high-intent searches.
194	
195	**Structural caveat:** These priors apply only when the query-origination behaviour is structurally stable. If Search query share migrates because users adopt AI assistants as their primary discovery layer — the interface-displacement failure mode — the historical mean-reversion priors do not apply. The recovery mechanism in prior episodes was mean-reverting ad economics, not mean-reverting user behaviour. Interface displacement would break the recovery mechanism itself: there is no historical precedent for Google recovering from durable query-origination share loss to a competing interface. The 2023 Bing episode is the closest analogue, and its resolution (Bing share gains marginalised) cannot be reliably extrapolated to a scenario where AI assistants are natively integrated at the OS, browser, and search-bar level at scale.

Episodes with non-numeric recovery (e.g. \"Partial\", \"Ongoing\") render as hollow circles at `cx = 478` with class `.p-sc-partial`. Each circle has a `<title>` child naming the episode. 226	      <p><strong>Revenue driver mechanics:</strong></p>
227	      <ol>
228	        <li><strong>Search:</strong> Paid clicks × CPC (Cost Per Click). Absolute quarterly Search CPM (Cost Per Thousand Impressions) and click volumes are not disclosed by Alphabet (noted as OQ6 gap in the engagement-KPI map) — revenue-per-search trend is inferred from total Search &amp; Other revenue YoY, not directly observable. This limits the precision of monetisation-compression monitoring; the playbook does not attempt quarterly KPI tracking.</li>
229	        <li><strong>YouTube:</strong> Primarily video ad auction (CPM-based); YouTube Premium subs add a lower-variance recurring line. Ad load and engagement trends are disclosed directionally but not with unit-economics granularity.</li>
230	        <li><strong>Cloud:</strong> Committed GCP revenue backlog + Workspace seats. Backlog growth is disclosed quarterly; it is the leading indicator for Cloud revenue trajectory.</li>
231	        <li><strong>Other Bets:</strong> Waymo is the only Other Bets asset with a plausible near-term monetisation path (robotaxi per-mile revenue, fleet licensing). Not material to DCF (Discounted Cash Flow) in the base case.</li>
232	      </ol>
233	
234	      <h3 id="end-market-exposure">End-market exposure</h3>
235	      <ul>
236	        <li><strong>Digital advertising (~77% of revenue):</strong> Cyclical sensitivity to global ad-spend budgets; secular tail risk from AI-interface displacement.</li>
237	        <li><strong>Enterprise cloud (~13% of revenue):</strong> GCP + Workspace; less cyclical; differentiated through Gemini integration.</li>
238	        <li><strong>Hardware / consumer services (~5%):</strong> Pixel, Google One, Maps API — limited operating leverage.</li>
239	      </ul>
240	    </section>
241	
242	    <section class="s" id="ai-investment-cycle-position">
243	      <header><span class="ix">02</span><h2>AI Investment Cycle Position</h2></header>
244	
245	      <p>Alphabet spent ~$91B in FY2025 capex, ~70% AI-attributed per public guidance. This depresses TTM clean FCF margin and creates a two-sided uncertainty that is structurally different from a normal capex cycle trough: the normalisation path depends on <strong>which of two competing margin theses proves correct.</strong></p>
246	
247	      <p><strong>Path A — cost-temporary (base case):</strong><br>
248	      AI model efficiency improves on hardware and software curves (inference cost-per-query falls as TPUs scale and model compression matures). Capex-as-share-of-revenue mean-reverts post-2027 as the build phase completes. Monetisation density per AI-assisted query holds near current levels or improves (AI Overviews maintain ad slots; AI Mode monetises at comparable RPM (Revenue Per Mille) to standard Search). Terminal margin recovers toward 30% SBC-stripped FCF.</p>
249	
250	      <p><strong>Path B — cost-permanent (bear-case terminal margin thesis):</strong><br>
251	      AI serving costs do not decay with scale at the rate Path A assumes — either because competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment, or because each AI query is structurally more compute-intensive than a traditional lookup. Simultaneously, AI-style answering reduces click-through rates, compressing ad density and CPC. Revenue growth decelerates while cost stays elevated. Terminal margin stabilises in the low-20s. This is the basis for <code>scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22</code>.</p>
252	
253	      <p><strong>Base-case choice:</strong> The playbook picks Path A but does not assume the asymmetry away. The <code>terminal_margin</code> base of 30% reflects Path A prevailing. The bear <code>scenario_axes</code> captures Path B as a discrete scenario — not a symmetric delta from base — because interface displacement and cost-permanence cause joint compression of both growth and margin simultaneously, which a symmetric ±multiplier cannot represent.</p>
254	
255	      <p><strong>Normalised-margin anchors:</strong> The <code>terminal_margin</code> base of 30% sits between two reference points. Reported TTM FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin is severely depressed by the AI build cycle — with ~$91B FY2025 capex, capex-blended group FCF margin is in the low-to-mid single digits (approximate; derived from disclosed capex and operating cash flows). On a normalised-capex, SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped basis — stripping the AI-attributed ~$64B capex increment above estimated pre-AI maintenance capex (~$25B) and SBC (~5–6% of revenue per disclosed annual figures) — clean FCF margin is inferred at approximately 22–27%: this is the distressed-floor reference point under Path A's recovery thesis. Search-segment-implied margin is structurally higher: Search &amp; Other at ~57% of revenue is Alphabet's highest-margin segment, with implied margins above 35% plausible given disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income of ~28–30% (approximate; GAAP segment FCF margins are not separately reported — treat these as order-of-magnitude anchors, not precise figures). The 30% base sits between the normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%) and the Search-segment ceiling (~35%+) — a defensible midpoint under Path A.</p>
256	
257	      <p><strong>AI-capex normalisation signal:</strong> The evidence-gating condition for Path A is a sustained decline in capex/revenue ratio after FY2026, visible across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that re-elevates above FY2025 levels by FY2028 would be evidence for Path B.</p>

277	  <p>IBM (Installed Base Management) is the earnings-floor segment: service contracts and upgrades on the ~4,000-tool installed base continue regardless of new-system order cycles. It is the component most vulnerable to a China-service-rule tightening scenario (see Failure Modes).</p>
278	
279	  <h3 id="key-revenue-drivers">Key revenue drivers</h3>
280	  <ol>
281	    <li><strong>EUV unit shipments</strong> &#8212; the volume metric for leading-edge logic. Consensus expects a step-up to ~90&#8211;100 units/year by 2027 from ~50&#8211;60 in 2024; below-60 for two consecutive years is a bearish inflection signal.</li>
282	    <li><strong>High-NA EUV ramp</strong> &#8212; ASP (Average Selling Price) per High-NA tool is ~&#8364;350M vs ~&#8364;200M for standard EUV. Even 5 additional High-NA units/year moves blended ASP materially. First customer is TSMC; Intel and Samsung are expected second/third.</li>
283	    <li><strong>China revenue share</strong> &#8212; ranged 20&#8211;49% of system revenue (2022&#8211;2023 peak) before export-control restrictions; tracking ~15&#8211;20% under current rules. Further rule tightening is the bear-case revenue risk; stabilisation at current levels is the base case.</li>
284	    <li><strong>IBM attach rate</strong> &#8212; services revenue as % of cumulative installed base value. Rising attach rate signals customer utilisation and confidence; falling attach rate (e.g., from China service restrictions) is the canary in the earnings-floor thesis.</li>
285	  </ol>
286	
287	  <h3 id="end-market-exposure">End-market exposure</h3>
288	  <ul>
289	    <li><strong>Leading-edge logic (HPC/AI + smartphones):</strong> TSMC, Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry &#8212; drive EUV and High-NA demand</li>
290	    <li><strong>Memory (DRAM + NAND):</strong> SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung Memory &#8212; drive EUV-for-DRAM and advanced-patterning demand</li>
291	    <li><strong>Mature logic / specialty:</strong> auto, industrial, IoT via mature DUV (less cyclically exposed but not immune)</li>
292	  </ul>

295	  </div>
296	</section>
297

301	  <h2>2. Capex-Cycle Position</h2>
302	  <p>ASML is in a <strong>cycle-trough / inflection</strong> phase as of mid-2026. The 2024&#8211;2025 digestion period (customers pausing orders after COVID-era over-ordering of DUV tools) is expected to trough in 2026, with re-acceleration in 2027&#8211;2029 on two overlapping drivers:</p>
303	  <ol>
304	    <li><strong>AI-driven advanced-node demand:</strong> TSMC N2/N2P, Samsung 2GAP, Intel 18A ramps require sustained EUV intensity. Hyperscaler custom-silicon fabs (Google, Meta, Amazon) are incremental new demand on top of smartphone-driven baseline.</li>

65	## 2. AI Investment Cycle Position
66	
67	Alphabet spent ~$91B in FY2025 capex, ~70% AI-attributed per public guidance. This depresses TTM clean FCF margin and creates a two-sided uncertainty that is structurally different from a normal capex cycle trough: the normalisation path depends on **which of two competing margin theses proves correct.**
68	
69	**Path A — cost-temporary (base case):**  
70	AI model efficiency improves on hardware and software curves (inference cost-per-query falls as TPUs scale and model compression matures). Capex-as-share-of-revenue mean-reverts post-2027 as the build phase completes. Monetisation density per AI-assisted query holds near current levels or improves (AI Overviews maintain ad slots; AI Mode monetises at comparable RPM (Revenue Per Mille) to standard Search). Terminal margin recovers toward 30% SBC-stripped FCF.
71	
72	**Path B — cost-permanent (bear-case terminal margin thesis):**  
73	AI serving costs do not decay with scale at the rate Path A assumes — either because competitive pressure forces continued reinvestment, or because each AI query is structurally more compute-intensive than a traditional lookup. Simultaneously, AI-style answering reduces click-through rates, compressing ad density and CPC. Revenue growth decelerates while cost stays elevated. Terminal margin stabilises in the low-20s. This is the basis for `scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.22`.
74	
75	**Base-case choice:** The playbook picks Path A but does not assume the asymmetry away. The `terminal_margin` base of 30% reflects Path A prevailing. The bear `scenario_axes` captures Path B as a discrete scenario — not a symmetric delta from base — because interface displacement and cost-permanence cause joint compression of both growth and margin simultaneously, which a symmetric ±multiplier cannot represent.
76	
77	**Normalised-margin anchors:** The `terminal_margin` base of 30% sits between two reference points. Reported TTM FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin is severely depressed by the AI build cycle — with ~$91B FY2025 capex, capex-blended group FCF margin is in the low-to-mid single digits (approximate; derived from disclosed capex and operating cash flows). On a normalised-capex, SBC (Stock-Based Compensation)-stripped basis — stripping the AI-attributed ~$64B capex increment above estimated pre-AI maintenance capex (~$25B) and SBC (~5–6% of revenue per disclosed annual figures) — clean FCF margin is inferred at approximately 22–27%: this is the distressed-floor reference point under Path A's recovery thesis. Search-segment-implied margin is structurally higher: Search & Other at ~57% of revenue is Alphabet's highest-margin segment, with implied margins above 35% plausible given disclosed Cloud and Other Bets operating losses offset against group operating income of ~28–30% (approximate; GAAP segment FCF margins are not separately reported — treat these as order-of-magnitude anchors, not precise figures). The 30% base sits between the normalised-FCF floor (~22–27%) and the Search-segment ceiling (~35%+) — a defensible midpoint under Path A.
78	
79	**AI-capex normalisation signal:** The evidence-gating condition for Path A is a sustained decline in capex/revenue ratio after FY2026, visible across two consecutive annual periods. A ratio that re-elevates above FY2025 levels by FY2028 would be evidence for Path B.

62	## 2. Capex-Cycle Position
63	
64	ASML is in a **cycle-trough / inflection** phase as of mid-2026. The 2024–2025 digestion period (customers pausing orders after COVID-era over-ordering of DUV tools) is expected to trough in 2026, with re-acceleration in 2027–2029 on two overlapping drivers:
65	
66	1. **AI-driven advanced-node demand:** TSMC N2/N2P, Samsung 2GAP, Intel 18A ramps require sustained EUV intensity. Hyperscaler custom-silicon fabs (Google, Meta, Amazon) are incremental new demand on top of smartphone-driven baseline.
67	2. **High-NA volume ramp:** First High-NA tools are being qualified at TSMC Arizona and Intel Ohio. If High-NA economics validate (cost-per-wafer clears vs multi-patterning DUV), the step-up in ASP per unit creates a revenue tailwind independent of unit-volume growth.
68	
69	**Normalised-margin thesis:** The `terminal_margin` override of 30% assumes High-NA reaches mature unit economics, customer utilisation normalises post-trough, and customer-prepayment working-capital swings dampen over a full cycle. TTM clean FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin (~24%) is trough-distorted by both the demand digestion period and ramp-related investment; anchoring the DCF on TTM understates steady-state. The 30% base sits between TTM clean FCF (~24%) and TTM earnings margin (~35%, implied by P/E 49.5 / P/S 17.18) — a defensible midpoint.
70	
71	**Bear case:** If High-NA economics fail to clear at scale OR if the semi cycle air-pocket is deeper than expected, utilisation stays weak and terminal margin compresses to TTM-clean levels. This is exactly what `scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.24` captures — it anchors the bear terminal margin at the observed trough rather than at a symmetric ±delta from base.
72	
73	**Cycle re-acceleration signal:** The evidence-gating condition for the base-case trough-and-re-acceleration thesis is three concurrent observables: (a) SEMI book-to-bill ratio sustained above 1.2 for ≥2 consecutive quarters; (b) ASML's quarterly earnings commentary guiding EUV unit shipments toward ≥70 units/year run-rate; (c) published guidance confirming the 2030 LRP (Long-Range Plan) envelope without downward revision at a Capital Markets Day event. A ratio that stays below 1.0 and LRP guidance that steps down by FY2028 would constitute evidence for the extended-digestion bear case rather than a V-shaped recovery.

32	## 1. Business Architecture
33	
34	### Segment mix (approximate FY2025 basis)
35	
36	| Segment | Revenue share | Growth trajectory |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| EUV systems (standard + High-NA) | ~50% | Cycle-dependent; High-NA ramp adds a step-up from 2026 |
39	| Advanced DUV (immersion) | ~25% | Mature; sensitive to logic node digestion pace |
40	| Mature DUV (dry, KrF, i-line) | ~10% | Stable; exposed to auto / industrial / mature-node capex |
41	| Installed Base Management (IBM) — services + upgrades | ~15% | Most defensive; ~25% of revenue; less cyclical than new tool orders |
42	
43	IBM (Installed Base Management) is the earnings-floor segment: service contracts and upgrades on the ~4,000-tool installed base continue regardless of new-system order cycles. It is the component most vulnerable to a China-service-rule tightening scenario (see Failure Modes).
44	
45	### Key revenue drivers
46	
47	1. **EUV unit shipments** — the volume metric for leading-edge logic. Consensus expects a step-up to ~90–100 units/year by 2027 from ~50–60 in 2024; below-60 for two consecutive years is a bearish inflection signal.
48	2. **High-NA EUV ramp** — ASP (Average Selling Price) per High-NA tool is ~€350M vs ~€200M for standard EUV. Even 5 additional High-NA units/year moves blended ASP materially. First customer is TSMC; Intel and Samsung are expected second/third.
49	3. **China revenue share** — ranged 20–49% of system revenue (2022–2023 peak) before export-control restrictions; tracking ~15–20% under current rules. Further rule tightening is the bear-case revenue risk; stabilisation at current levels is the base case.
50	4. **IBM attach rate** — services revenue as % of cumulative installed base value. Rising attach rate signals customer utilisation and confidence; falling attach rate (e.g., from China service restrictions) is the canary in the earnings-floor thesis.

Tick position = `(base − floor) / (ceiling − floor) × 100`.\n\n**HTML.**\n```html\n<figure class=\"p-band-fig\" role=\"img\"\n  aria-label=\"Normalised-margin range: floor ~{{floor}}%, base ~{{base}}%, ceiling ~{{ceiling}}%\">\n  <div class=\"p-band-row\">\n    <span class=\"p-band-ep\">~{{floor}}%<br><span class=\"p-band-ep-lbl\">floor</span></span>\n    <div class=\"p-band-track\">\n      <div class=\"p-band-tick\" style=\"left:{{tick_pct}}%\">\n        <span class=\"p-band-tick-lbl\">~{{base}}%</span>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n    <span class=\"p-band-ep p-band-ep-r\">~{{ceiling}}%<br><span class=\"p-band-ep-lbl\">ceiling</span></span>\n  </div>\n</figure>\n```\n\n**CSS.**\n```css\n.p-band-fig { margin: 0.5rem 0 0.75rem; }\n.p-band-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; }\n.p-band-ep { font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted); text-align: center; white-space: nowrap; min-width: 2.5rem; line-height: 1.3; }\n.p-band-ep-r { text-align: right; }\n.p-band-ep-lbl { font-size: 0.65rem; }\n.p-band-track { flex: 1; height: 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: linear-gradient(to right, var(--danger-soft), var(--warn-soft), var(--ok-soft)); position: relative; }\n.p-band-tick { position: absolute; top: -4px; width: 3px; height: 20px; background: var(--fg); border-radius: 2px; transform: translateX(-50%); }\n.p-band-tick-lbl { position: absolute; bottom: 24px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); white-space: nowrap; background: var(--bg); padding: 0 2px; }\n```\n\n**Accessibility.** The `<figure>` carries a full `aria-label` with all three values in plain text. The gradient is decorative — floor, base, and ceiling values are announced verbatim by the label.\n\n**When to use.** Playbook §2 sections that establish a floor-to-ceiling margin range with a named base anchor. Both GOOG §2 (\"AI Investment Cycle Position\") and ASML §2 (\"Capex-Cycle Position\") match. 361	<section id="capex-cycle-position">
362	  <h2>2. Capex-Cycle Position</h2>
363	  <p>ASML is in a <strong>cycle-trough / inflection</strong> phase as of mid-2026. The 2024&#8211;2025 digestion period (customers pausing orders after COVID-era over-ordering of DUV tools) is expected to trough in 2026, with re-acceleration in 2027&#8211;2029 on two overlapping drivers:</p>
364	  <ol>
365	    <li><strong>AI-driven advanced-node demand:</strong> TSMC N2/N2P, Samsung 2GAP, Intel 18A ramps require sustained EUV intensity. Hyperscaler custom-silicon fabs (Google, Meta, Amazon) are incremental new demand on top of smartphone-driven baseline.</li>
366	    <li><strong>High-NA volume ramp:</strong> First High-NA tools are being qualified at TSMC Arizona and Intel Ohio. If High-NA economics validate (cost-per-wafer clears vs multi-patterning DUV), the step-up in ASP per unit creates a revenue tailwind independent of unit-volume growth.</li>
367	  </ol>
368	  <p><strong>Normalised-margin thesis:</strong> The <code>terminal_margin</code> override of 30% assumes High-NA reaches mature unit economics, customer utilisation normalises post-trough, and customer-prepayment working-capital swings dampen over a full cycle. TTM clean FCF (Free Cash Flow) margin (~24%) is trough-distorted; anchoring the DCF on TTM understates steady-state. The 30% base sits between TTM clean FCF (~24%) and TTM earnings margin (~35%, implied by P/E 49.5 / P/S 17.18) &#8212; a defensible midpoint.</p>
369	  <p><strong>Bear case:</strong> If High-NA economics fail to clear at scale OR if the semi cycle air-pocket is deeper than expected, utilisation stays weak and terminal margin compresses to TTM-clean levels. This is exactly what <code>scenario_axes.bear.terminal_margin: 0.24</code> captures &#8212; it anchors the bear terminal margin at the observed trough rather than at a symmetric &#177;delta from base.</p>
